sentences.zh: 梁書卷第二十一 列傳第十五

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 21, Biographies 15
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 21, Biographies 15

sentences.zh: 王瞻 王志 王峻 王暕 子訓 王泰 王份 孫鍚 僉 張充 柳惲 蔡撙 江蒨

translations.literal: Wang Zhan, Wang Zhi, Wang Jun, Wang Jian, Wang Xun, Wang Tai, Wang Fen, Wang Yang, Zhang Chong, Liu Yun, Cai Zun, Jiang Qian
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan, Wang Zhi, Wang Jun, Wang Jian, Wang Xun, Wang Tai, Wang Fen, Wang Yang, Zhang Chong, Liu Yun, Cai Zun, and Jiang Qian

sentences.zh: 王瞻字思範，琅邪臨沂人，宋太保弘從孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhan, styled Sifan, was a man of Linyi in Langya and a great-nephew of Wang Hong, Grand Tutor of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan, whose style was Sifan, came from Linyi in Langya and was a great-nephew of Wang Hong, Grand Tutor under the Song.

sentences.zh: 祖柳，光祿大夫、東亭侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Liu was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Marquis of Dongting.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liu had served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and held the title Marquis of Dongting.

sentences.zh: 父猷，廷尉卿。

translations.literal: His father You was Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father You had been Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 瞻年數歲，嘗從師受業，時有伎經其門，同學皆出觀，瞻獨不視，習誦如初。

translations.literal: When Zhan was only a few years old, he once studied under a teacher. Performers passed his gate, and all his classmates went out to watch, but Zhan alone did not look and went on reciting his lesson as before.
translations.idiomatic: As a small boy Zhan was studying with a teacher when entertainers happened to pass the gate. Every classmate ran out to watch, but Zhan alone stayed at his desk and kept reciting as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 從父尚書僕射僧達聞而異之，謂瞻父曰：「吾宗不衰，寄之此子。

translations.literal: His father's younger cousin Wang Sengda, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, heard of this and was struck by it. He said to Zhan's father, "Our clan will not decline—we may entrust it to this boy."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sengda, a younger cousin of Zhan's father who served as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, heard the story and was astonished. He told Zhan's father, "Our house will not fade—we can pin our hopes on this child."

sentences.zh: 」年十二，居父憂，以孝聞。

translations.literal: At twelve he was in mourning for his father and became known for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he entered mourning for his father and won a reputation for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 服闋，襲封東亭侯。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he inherited the fief as Marquis of Dongting.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning ended, he succeeded to the title Marquis of Dongting.

sentences.zh: 瞻幼時輕薄，好逸遊，爲閭里所患。

translations.literal: In youth Zhan was frivolous and fond of roaming for pleasure, to the vexation of his neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Zhan was flighty and loved idle wandering, which troubled everyone in the neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗折節有士操，涉獵書記，於朞射尤善。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he greatly restrained himself and showed the bearing of a gentleman, read widely in books and records, and was especially skilled at board games and archery.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he sharply reined himself in and cultivated the manners of a gentleman, read widely, and excelled above all at chess and archery.

sentences.zh: 起家著作佐郎，累遷太子舍人、太尉主簿、太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He began his career as an Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat, and was promoted in succession to Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant, and Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat, then rose through Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent, chief clerk to the Grand Commandant, and Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出爲鄱陽內史，秩滿，授太子中舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as Administrator of Poyang. When his term ended he was appointed Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent in the central government.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was posted as Administrator of Poyang; when his term expired he returned to court as Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 又爲齊南海王友，尋轉司徒竟陵王從事中郎，王甚相賓禮。

translations.literal: He next served as Companion to the Prince of Nanhai of Qi, and soon transferred to Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat of Prince Jingling of the Sikong, whom he greatly honored and treated with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He next became a companion to Qi’s Prince of Nanhai, then moved to Attendant Gentleman on the staff of Prince Jingling of the Sikong, who treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 南海王爲護軍將軍，瞻爲長史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nanhai became General Who Guards the Army, Zhan became his Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Nanhai was made General Who Guards the Army, Zhan served as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 又出補徐州別駕從事史，遷驃騎將軍王晏長史。

translations.literal: He went out again as Assistant Administrator of Xuzhou, then was promoted to Chief Clerk to General of Agile Cavalry Wang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted again as assistant administrator of Xuzhou, then promoted to chief clerk to Wang Yan, General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 晏誅，出爲晉陵太守。

translations.literal: When Yan was executed, Zhan went out as Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan was put to death, Zhan was sent out as Administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 瞻潔己爲政，妻子不免饑寒。

translations.literal: Zhan kept himself pure in government, and even his wife and children did not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan governed with austere integrity; even his wife and children knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 時大司馬王敬則舉兵作亂，路經晉陵，郡民多附敬則。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Marshal Wang Jingze raised troops in rebellion and passed through Jinling. Many people in the commandery joined Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Marshal Wang Jingze rebelled and marched through Jinling, and many in the commandery rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 軍敗，臺軍討賊黨，瞻言於朝曰：「愚人易動，不足窮法。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated, the imperial forces punished the rebels' associates. Zhan said to the court, "Simple people are easily stirred; they should not be pursued to the full rigor of the law."
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, the central armies set about punishing collaborators. Zhan pleaded at court, "Ordinary folk are easily swayed; the law need not be pressed to its utmost against them."

sentences.zh: 」明帝許之，所全活者萬數。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming approved this, and the number he thereby spared ran into the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming agreed, and tens of thousands of lives were spared.

sentences.zh: 徵拜給事黃門侍郎，撫軍建安王長史，御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Army, Prince of Jian'an, and Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, chief clerk to Prince Jian'an, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 高祖霸府開，以瞻爲大司馬相國諮議參軍，領錄事。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor opened his Chief Minister's headquarters, he made Zhan Consulting Adjutant in the Chief Minister's office and Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu opened his chief minister's headquarters, he appointed Zhan Consulting Adjutant and Recorder.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，爲侍中，遷左民尚書，俄轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established, he became Attendant Gentleman and was promoted to Minister of the Left for the People, and soon transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: With the founding of Liang he became Attendant Gentleman, then Minister of the Left for the People, and soon Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 瞻性率亮，居選部，所舉多行其意。

translations.literal: Zhan was by nature frank and bright. In the Ministry of Personnel, most of those he recommended were men who suited his own judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was candid and open by nature. At the Ministry of Personnel he usually advanced candidates who matched his own preferences.

sentences.zh: 頗嗜酒，每飲或竟日，而精神益朗贍，不廢簿領。

translations.literal: He was quite fond of wine and would sometimes drink for whole days at a stretch, yet his spirit grew only clearer and more vigorous, and he did not neglect his paperwork.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and might drink all day long, yet his mind only grew sharper and his paperwork never slipped.

sentences.zh: 高祖每稱瞻有三術，射、朞、酒也。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor often said that Zhan had three arts: archery, board games, and wine.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor used to say Zhan possessed three arts—archery, chess, and drinking.

sentences.zh: 尋加左軍將軍，以疾不拜，仍爲侍中，領驍騎將軍，未拜，卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title General of the Left Army, but because of illness he did not accept it. He remained Attendant Gentleman and was to head the General of Valiant Cavalry, but before he took office he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon offered the additional post of General of the Left Army but declined it on grounds of illness. He remained Attendant Gentleman and was slated to command the General of Valiant Cavalry, but died before taking up the appointment, at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 諡康侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Marquis Kang.

sentences.zh: 子長玄，著作佐郎，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Changxuan was an Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changxuan served as Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat and died young.

sentences.zh: 王志字次道，琅邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, styled Cidao, was a man of Linyi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, whose style was Cidao, came from Linyi in Langya.

sentences.zh: 祖曇首，宋左光祿大夫、豫寧文侯；

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan Shou was Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Marquis Wen of Yuning.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tan Shou had been Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Marquis Wen of Yuning.

sentences.zh: 父僧虔，齊司空、簡穆公：並有重名。

translations.literal: His father Sengqian was Sikong and Duke Jianmu of Qi—both men of great renown.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengqian had been Sikong and Duke Jianmu of Qi; both generations enjoyed great fame.

sentences.zh: 志年九歲，居所生母憂，哀容毀瘠，爲中表所異。

translations.literal: At nine Zhi was in mourning for his birth mother. His grieving countenance was so wasted that his cousins and in-laws were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he mourned his birth mother; his grief was so haggard that kinsmen and in-laws marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，選尚孝武女安固公主，拜駙馬都尉、秘書郎。

translations.literal: In his early twenties he was chosen to marry Emperor Xiaowu's daughter, Princess Angu, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards and Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he was matched to Emperor Xiaowu's daughter, Princess Angu, and appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards and Secretary.

sentences.zh: 累遷太尉行參軍，太子舍人，武陵王文學。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Acting Gentleman in the Grand Commandant's office, Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and Literary Adjunct to the Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through acting gentleman in the Grand Commandant's office, Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and literary adjunct to the Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 褚淵爲司徒，引志爲主簿。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan was made Sikong and brought Zhi in as his Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu Yuan became Sikong he took Zhi on as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 淵謂僧虔曰：「朝廷之恩，本爲殊特，所可光榮，在屈賢子。

translations.literal: Yuan said to Sengqian, "The court's favor was meant to be extraordinary; what can bring honor to your house is that it bends to employ your worthy son."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan told Sengqian, "The court's grace was meant to be exceptional; the glory of your house lies in bending high rank to employ your worthy son."

sentences.zh: 」累遷鎮北竟陵王功曹史、安陸南郡二王友。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Recorder in the Prince of Jingling's staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Companion to the Princes of Anlu and Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted through recorder on Prince Jingling's staff, then companion to the princes of Anlu and Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 入爲中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋除宣城內史，清謹有恩惠。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Administrator of Xuancheng, where he was scrupulous and kindly.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as Administrator of Xuancheng, governing with scrupulous care and humane kindness.

sentences.zh: 郡民張倪、吳慶爭田，經年不決。

translations.literal: The people Zhang Ni and Wu Qing disputed a field and could not settle it for years.
translations.idiomatic: Two villagers, Zhang Ni and Wu Qing, had quarreled over a field for years without resolution.

sentences.zh: 志到官，父老乃相謂曰：「王府君有德政，吾曹鄉里乃有此爭。

translations.literal: When Zhi arrived, the elders said to one another, "Magistrate Wang governs with virtue—how can our neighborhood still have such a dispute?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi took office, the elders said among themselves, "Magistrate Wang rules with virtue—how can we still be fighting like this?"

sentences.zh: 」倪、慶因相攜請罪，所訟地遂爲閑田。

translations.literal: Ni and Qing therefore went together to ask forgiveness, and the land they had sued over became idle ground.
translations.idiomatic: Ni and Qing went together to beg pardon, and the contested land was left fallow between them.

sentences.zh: 徵拜黃門侍郎，尋遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and soon promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and soon made Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、東陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 郡獄有重囚十餘人，冬至日悉遣還家，過節皆返，惟一人失期，獄司以爲言。

translations.literal: There were more than ten serious criminals in the prison. On the winter solstice he sent them all home; all returned after the holiday except one who was late, and the prison staff reported it.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten serious offenders sat in the jail. On the winter solstice he sent them home for the holiday; all returned on time except one, and the jailers reported the breach.

sentences.zh: 志曰：「此自太守事，主者勿憂。

translations.literal: Zhi said, "This is the magistrate's affair; you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "That is the magistrate's concern, not yours."

sentences.zh: 」明旦，果自詣獄，辭以婦孕，吏民益嘆服之。

translations.literal: The next morning the man indeed came to the prison of his own accord, explaining that his wife was pregnant. Officials and commoners admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning the man appeared at the jail and explained that his wife was pregnant. Officials and people admired Zhi all the more.

sentences.zh: 視事三年，齊永明二年，入爲侍中，未拜，轉吏部尚書，在選以和理稱。

translations.literal: After three years in office, in the second year of Yongming of Qi he entered the capital as Attendant Gentleman. Before he took office he was transferred to Minister of Personnel, where he was praised for fair and orderly selection.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he entered the capital as Attendant Gentleman in the second year of Yongming. Before he assumed the post he was moved to Minister of Personnel, where his appointments won praise for fairness.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景平，以例加右軍將軍，封臨汝侯，固讓不受，改領右衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing was pacified, he received by precedent the additional title General of the Right Army and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linru, but firmly declined and would not accept; he was changed to command the Right Guard instead.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Huijing's rebellion was crushed he was offered, by precedent, the additional post of General of the Right Army and enfeoffment as Marquis of Linru, but firmly declined both and was made commander of the Right Guard instead.

sentences.zh: 義師至，城內害東昏，百僚署名送其首。

translations.literal: When the righteous army arrived, those inside the city killed Dong Hun, and the hundred officials signed their names to send forward his head.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army reached the capital, the men inside the city killed Dong Hun, and every official signed a memorial forwarding his head.

sentences.zh: 志聞而歎曰：「冠雖弊，可加足乎？

translations.literal: When Zhi heard this he sighed and said, "Even if the cap is worn out, may one still put it on his feet?"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Zhi sighed and said, "Even a worn-out cap—can you wear it on your feet?"

sentences.zh: 」因取庭中樹葉挪服之，偽悶，不署名。

translations.literal: He therefore took leaves from the courtyard tree and held them in his mouth, feigning distress, and did not sign.
translations.idiomatic: He took leaves from the courtyard tree, clenched them in his mouth as if ill, and refused to sign.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽箋無志署，心嘉之，弗以讓也。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, reading the memorial, saw that Zhi's name was not there, admired him in his heart, and did not press the matter of his earlier refusal.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor read the memorial and saw Zhi's name missing, he admired him inwardly and did not revisit his earlier refusal of honors.

sentences.zh: 霸府開，以志爲右軍將軍、驃騎大將軍長史。

translations.literal: When the Chief Minister's headquarters was opened, Zhi was made General of the Right Army and Chief Clerk to the General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister's headquarters opened, Zhi became General of the Right Army and chief clerk to the General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，遷散騎常侍、中書令。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established, he was promoted to Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: With the founding of Liang he was promoted to Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 志善草隸，當時以爲楷法。

translations.literal: Zhi was skilled in cursive and clerical script and was regarded at the time as a model of the art.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi excelled at cursive and clerical script and was regarded in his day as the standard of calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 齊遊擊將軍徐希秀亦號能書，常謂志爲「書聖」。

translations.literal: Xu Xixiu, General Who Roams in Attack of Qi, was also famed for writing and often called Zhi the "sage of calligraphy."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xixiu of Qi, General Who Roams in Attack, was also celebrated for calligraphy and often called Zhi the "sage of writing."

sentences.zh: 志家世居建康禁中里馬蕃巷，父僧虔以來，門風多寬恕，志尤惇厚。

translations.literal: The Wang family for generations lived in Mafan Lane inside the forbidden quarter of Jiankang. Since the time of his father Sengqian the household style had been forgiving, and Zhi was especially sincere and generous.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the Wangs had lived in Mafan Lane within Jiankang's palace quarter. Since his father Sengqian's day the family had been indulgent by habit, and Zhi was especially warm and magnanimous.

sentences.zh: 所歷職，不以罪咎劾人。

translations.literal: In every post he held he did not impeach people for faults and crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he held he never impeached subordinates for faults or crimes.

sentences.zh: 門下客嘗盜脫志車憲賣之，志知而不問，待之如初。

translations.literal: A client once secretly removed the canopy of Zhi's carriage and sold it. Zhi knew but did not question him and treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: A retainer once stole the canopy from Zhi's carriage and sold it. Zhi knew but said nothing and treated him exactly as before.

sentences.zh: 賓客遊其門者，專覆其過而稱其善。

translations.literal: Guests who visited his gate would cover up his faults and praise his virtues.
translations.idiomatic: Guests at his door always glossed over his faults and spoke only of his virtues.

sentences.zh: 兄弟子侄皆篤實謙和，時人號馬蕃諸王爲長者。

translations.literal: Brothers, sons, and nephews were all solid, modest, and gentle, and people of the time called the Wangs of Mafan Lane "the elders."
translations.idiomatic: Brothers, sons, and nephews were all steady, modest, and mild, and contemporaries called the Wangs of Mafan Lane "the elders."

sentences.zh: 普通四年，志改葬，高祖厚賻賜之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Putong, Zhi had his burial place changed, and the High Ancestor richly rewarded and bestowed gifts on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Putong, when Zhi moved his ancestral graves, the High Ancestor lavished gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 追諡曰安。

translations.literal: He was posthumously titled An.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name An.

sentences.zh: 有五子緝、休、諲、操、素，並知名。

translations.literal: He had five sons—Ji, Xiu, Yin, Cao, and Su—all of whom became well known.
translations.idiomatic: He left five sons—Ji, Xiu, Yin, Cao, and Su—each of whom won renown.

sentences.zh: 王峻字茂遠，琅邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Wang Jun, styled Maoyuan, was a man of Linyi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, whose style was Maoyuan, came from Linyi in Langya.

sentences.zh: 曾祖敬弘，有重名於宋世，位至左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jing Hong enjoyed great fame in the Song period and rose to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with credentials equal to those of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jing Hong had been greatly esteemed under the Song and rose to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 祖瓚之，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zan Zhi was Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zan Zhi had held the rank of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 父秀之，吳興太守。

translations.literal: His father Xiu Zhi was Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiu Zhi had been Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 峻少美風姿，善舉止。

translations.literal: Jun in his youth had a fine appearance and graceful bearing.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Jun was handsome and carried himself with grace.

sentences.zh: 起家著作佐郎，不拜，累遷中軍廬陵王法曹行參軍，太子舍人，邵陵王文學，太傅主簿。

translations.literal: He began his career as Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat but did not accept the post. He was promoted in succession to Acting Gentleman in the Law Bureau of Prince Luling of the Central Army, Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Literary Adjunct to the Prince of Shaoling, and Chief Clerk to the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat but declined. He then rose through acting gentleman in Prince Luling's law bureau, Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent, literary adjunct to the Prince of Shaoling, and chief clerk to the Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 府主齊竟陵王子良甚相賞遇。

translations.literal: His lord, Prince Jingling of Qi, greatly appreciated and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jingling of Qi, his patron, valued and favored him highly.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒主簿，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chief Clerk in the Sikong's office and left his post to observe mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to chief clerk in the Sikong's office, then left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除太子洗馬，建安王友。

translations.literal: When the mourning ended he was made Groom of the Heir Apparent and Companion to the Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became Groom of the Heir Apparent and companion to the Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧遠將軍、桂陽內史。

translations.literal: He went out as General of Far Pacification and Administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as General of Far Pacification and Administrator of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 會義師起，上流諸郡多相驚擾，峻閉門靜坐，一郡帖然，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, the commanderies upriver were mostly alarmed and disturbed, but Jun shut his gates and sat in quiet, and the whole commandery remained calm; the people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, commanderies upriver panicked, but Jun closed his gates and sat in stillness until the whole region stayed calm and the people trusted him.

sentences.zh: 天監初，還，除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he returned and was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianjian he returned to court as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚悅其風采，與陳郡謝覽同見賞擢。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor was very pleased with his bearing and promoted him together with Xie Lan of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor delighted in his bearing and advanced him together with Xie Lan of Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 俄遷吏部，當官不稱職，轉征虜安成王長史，又爲太子中庶子、遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, where he did not distinguish himself in office, and was made Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Prince of Ancheng, then Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent and General Who Roams in Attack.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he moved to the Ministry of Personnel, where he proved undistinguished, then became chief clerk to Prince Ancheng, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, and later Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent and General Who Roams in Attack.

sentences.zh: 出爲宣城太守，爲政清和，吏民安之。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xuancheng, where his government was pure and gentle and officials and people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Xuancheng, where he governed with clarity and kindness until officials and people alike were content.

sentences.zh: 視事三年，徵拜侍中，遷度支尚書。

translations.literal: After three years in office he was summoned as Attendant Gentleman and promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was recalled as Attendant Gentleman and promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又以本官兼起部尚書，監起太極殿。

translations.literal: He also held his former post concurrently as Minister for Palace Construction and supervised the building of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: He retained his former rank while concurrently serving as Minister for Palace Construction and overseeing the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 事畢，出爲征遠將軍、平西長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: When the work was finished he went out as General Who Pacifies the Distance, Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the West, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the project was finished he was posted as General Who Pacifies the Distance, chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the West, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋爲智武將軍、鎮西長史、蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General of Manifest Martial Power, Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the West, and Administrator of Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became General of Manifest Martial Power, chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the West, and Administrator of Shu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 還爲左民尚書，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Minister of the Left for the People and concurrently Colonel of the Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was made Minister of the Left for the People and concurrently Colonel of the Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，處選甚得名譽。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel, where his handling of selection won a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Minister of Personnel, where his appointments earned high praise.

sentences.zh: 峻性詳雅，無趨競心。

translations.literal: Jun was by nature refined and elegant and had no mind for scrambling after advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was refined and unhurried by nature and never scrambled for promotion.

sentences.zh: 嘗與謝覽約，官至侍中，不復謀進仕。

translations.literal: He once agreed with Xie Lan that when they reached Attendant Gentleman they would seek no further advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He once agreed with Xie Lan that once they reached Attendant Gentleman they would pursue no higher office.

sentences.zh: 覽自吏部尚書出爲吳興郡，平心不畏強禦，亦由處世之情旣薄故也。

translations.literal: Lan went out from Minister of Personnel to be Administrator of Wuxing. He judged cases impartially and did not fear the powerful, yet this too came from his having grown indifferent to worldly concerns.
translations.idiomatic: Lan left the Ministry of Personnel to govern Wuxing, judging cases fairly without fearing the powerful—yet that too sprang from his indifference to worldly ambition.

sentences.zh: 峻爲侍中以後，雖不退身，亦淡然自守，無所營務。

translations.literal: After Jun became Attendant Gentleman, although he did not withdraw from public life, he remained calmly self-contained and undertook no schemes.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun became Attendant Gentleman he did not retire, yet lived with quiet self-restraint and undertook no intrigues.

sentences.zh: 久之，以疾表解職，遷金紫光祿大夫，未拜。

translations.literal: After a long time he submitted a memorial on grounds of illness asking to leave office and was transferred to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, but did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he memorialized on grounds of illness to resign and was offered Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, but never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Putong he died.

sentences.zh: 時年五十六，諡惠子。

translations.literal: He was fifty-six years old and was given the posthumous title Marquis Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-six; his posthumous title was Marquis Hui.

sentences.zh: 子琮，玩。

translations.literal: His sons were Cong and Wan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Cong and Wan.

sentences.zh: 琮爲國子生，尚始興王女繁昌縣主，不慧，爲學生所嗤，遂離婚。

translations.literal: Cong was a student at the Imperial University, married the daughter of the Prince of Shixing, Princess of Fanchang, but was dull-witted and was mocked by his fellow students, so the marriage was dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Cong studied at the Imperial University and married the daughter of the Prince of Shixing, Princess of Fanchang, but proved dull-witted, was ridiculed by his classmates, and the marriage was annulled.

sentences.zh: 峻謝王，王曰：「此自上意，僕極不願如此。

translations.literal: Jun apologized to the prince. The prince said, "This came from higher authority; I myself was most unwilling for it to happen."
translations.idiomatic: Jun apologized to the prince, who replied, "That order came from above; I myself was utterly unwilling."

sentences.zh: 」峻曰：「臣太祖是謝仁祖外孫，亦不藉殿下姻媾爲門戶。」

translations.literal: Jun said, "My great-grandfather was the maternal grandson of Xie Renzu; our house does not rely on Your Highness's marriage alliance for its standing."
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "My great-grandfather was the maternal grandson of Xie Renzu; our family does not need Your Highness's marriage tie to uphold its gate."

sentences.zh: 王暕字思晦，琅邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Wang Jian, styled Sihui, was a man of Linyi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, whose style was Sihui, came from Linyi in Langya.

sentences.zh: 父儉，齊太尉，南昌文憲公。

translations.literal: His father Jian was Grand Tutor of Qi and Duke Wenxian of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian had been Grand Tutor of Qi and Duke Wenxian of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 暕年數歲，而風神警拔，有成人之度。

translations.literal: Even at a few years of age, Jian's spirit was alert and outstanding, with the bearing of an adult.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood his manner was keen and commanding, with the composure of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 時文憲作宰，賓客盈門，見暕相謂曰：「公才公望，復在此矣。

translations.literal: At that time Duke Wenxian was chief minister and his gate was full of guests. Seeing Jian, they said to one another, "Your talent and your reputation have appeared again in this boy."
translations.idiomatic: While Duke Wenxian still held the chief ministry, guests filled his hall. When they saw Jian they said among themselves, "Your talent and stature live again in this child."

sentences.zh: 」弱冠，選尚淮南長公主，拜駙馬都尉，除員外散騎侍郎，不拜，改授晉安王文學，遷廬陵王友、秘書丞。

translations.literal: In his early twenties he was chosen to marry the Princess of Huainan, was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, and made Extraordinary Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry but did not accept. He was reassigned as Literary Adjunct to the Prince of Jin'an, then promoted to Companion to the Prince of Luling and Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he was matched to the Princess of Huainan, appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, and offered Extraordinary Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, which he declined. He became literary adjunct to the Prince of Jin'an, then companion to the Prince of Luling and Secretary.

sentences.zh: 明帝詔求異士，始安王遙光表薦暕及東海王僧孺曰：「臣聞求賢暫勞，垂拱永逸，方之疏壤，取類導川。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming issued an edict seeking men of unusual ability. The Prince of Shi'an, Yaoguang, memorialized recommending Jian and Wang Sengru of Donghai, saying: "Your servant has heard that to seek the worthy brings brief toil but enduring ease when one folds the hands in rule—like piling earth on a dyke, it belongs to the same class as guiding a stream."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming ordered a search for extraordinary talent. Prince Shi'an, Yaoguang, memorialized recommending Jian and Wang Sengru of Donghai: "I have heard that seeking worthies costs brief labor but yields lasting ease under folded hands in government—as with raising a dike, it is of a piece with channeling a river."

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下道隱旒纊，信充符璽，白駒空谷，振鷺在庭；

translations.literal: Your Majesty's Way is hidden behind the tassels of the crown, yet trust fills the tally and seal; white colts stand in empty valleys, and herons in flight line the court—
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's Way is veiled behind the crown's tassels, yet trust fills the seals; white colts wait in empty valleys, and herons in flight throng the courtyard—

sentences.zh: 猶懼隱鱗卜祝，藏器屠保，物色關下，委裘河上。

translations.literal: yet one still fears hidden scales among diviners and butchers, talents concealed among slaughterers and grooms, men sought at the pass below, and a fur cloak cast upon the river.
translations.idiomatic: yet you still fear hidden dragons among diviners, talents buried with butchers and grooms, worthies sought at the gate, and a fur cloak left on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 非取制於一狐，諒求味於兼采。

translations.literal: It is not to take the measure from a single fox; one must surely seek flavor from many ingredients.
translations.idiomatic: You do not take your measure from one fox alone; you must gather flavor from many sources.

sentences.zh: 而五聲倦響，九工是詢；

translations.literal: Yet when the five tones grow weary, the nine craftsmen are consulted;
translations.idiomatic: When the five tones grow weary, the nine craftsmen are asked;

sentences.zh: 寢議廟堂，借聽輿皁。

translations.literal: deliberation in the ancestral temple borrows hearing from carriage and common cloth.
translations.idiomatic: counsel in the temple hall borrows hearing from carriage and commoner alike.

sentences.zh: 臣位任隆重，義兼邦家，實欲使名實不違，僥倖路絕。

translations.literal: Your servant's post is weighty and his duty embraces the state; he truly wishes that name and reality not diverge and that the path of luck be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: My post is weighty and my duty embraces the realm; I truly wish name and reality to match and the road of favoritism to be closed.

sentences.zh: 勢門上品，猶當格以清談；

translations.literal: Those of high rank in powerful houses should still be measured by pure discourse;
translations.idiomatic: Men of power in great houses should still be tested by pure discourse;

sentences.zh: 英俊下僚，不可限以位貌。

translations.literal: outstanding men among lower staff should not be limited by position and appearance.
translations.idiomatic: outstanding men among humble subordinates should not be barred by rank and looks.

sentences.zh: 竊見秘書丞琅邪王暕，年二十一，七葉重光，海內冠冕，神清氣茂，允迪中和。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed Secretary Wang Jian of Langya, aged twenty-one, seven generations of glory, the crown of the realm within the seas, with spirit clear and breath rich, truly treading the central Way.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed Wang Jian of Langya, Secretary, twenty-one years old, seven generations of glory, the foremost house under heaven, spirit clear and bearing ample, truly walking the middle Way.

sentences.zh: 叔寶理遣之談，彥輔名教之樂，故以暉映先達，領袖後進。

translations.literal: The discourses on principle of Shubao and the joy of name and teaching of Yanfu—thus he shines upon the men of old and leads the generation that follows.
translations.idiomatic: He has the discourses on principle of Shubao and the joy in name and teaching of Yanfu; he outshines the elders and leads the rising generation.

sentences.zh: 居無塵雜，家有賜書；

translations.literal: In dwelling, no dust or clutter; in his house, imperial gifts of books;
translations.idiomatic: His dwelling is free of vulgar dust; his house holds books granted by the throne;

sentences.zh: 辭賦清新，屬言玄遠；

translations.literal: his rhapsodies fresh and clear, his phrasing profound and far-reaching;
translations.idiomatic: his rhapsodies fresh and clear, his language subtle and far-reaching;

sentences.zh: 室邇人曠，物疏道親。

translations.literal: his rooms near yet men distant, things sparse yet the Way near.
translations.idiomatic: rooms close yet men far, things few yet the Way close.

sentences.zh: 養素丘園，台階虛位；

translations.literal: He nurtures simplicity in hill and garden while steps to the terrace stand empty;
translations.idiomatic: He cultivates simplicity in hill and garden while the steps to high office stand empty;

sentences.zh: 庠序公朝，萬夫傾首。

translations.literal: in the public school of the court, ten thousand men turn their heads.
translations.idiomatic: in the court's public school, ten thousand heads turn to him.

sentences.zh: 豈徒荀令可想，李公不亡而已哉！

translations.literal: Is he merely one whom Minister Xun might be compared to, or Lord Li not yet dead?
translations.idiomatic: Is he merely one to compare with Minister Xun, or proof that Lord Li has not died?

sentences.zh: 乃東序之秘寶，瑚璉之茂器。

translations.literal: He is a secret treasure of the eastern school, a splendid vessel of jade and bronze."
translations.idiomatic: He is a hidden treasure of the eastern hall, a splendid vessel of jade and bronze."

sentences.zh: 」除驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat of the General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman on the staff of the General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 訓字懷範，幼聰警有識量，徵士何胤見而奇之。

translations.literal: Xun, styled Huaifan, was in youth clever, alert, and of discernment. The recluse He Yin saw him and was struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, whose style was Huaifan, was clever and perceptive as a boy; the recluse He Yin saw him and marveled.

sentences.zh: 年十三，暕亡憂毀，家人莫之識。

translations.literal: At thirteen, when Jian died, his grief in mourning was so devastating that even his family did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, when Jian died, he mourned so fiercely that even his family hardly knew him.

sentences.zh: 十六，召見文德殿，應對爽徹。

translations.literal: At sixteen he was summoned to audience in the Hall of Cultivated Virtue and answered with bright clarity.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he was received in the Hall of Cultivated Virtue and answered with lucid grace.

sentences.zh: 上目送久之，顧謂朱异曰：「可謂相門有相矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor watched him leave for a long time, then turned and said to Zhu Yi, "One may truly say that a minister's house breeds ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor watched him go for a long while, then said to Zhu Yi, "Truly, a minister's house breeds ministers."

sentences.zh: 」補國子生，射策高第，除秘書郎，遷太子舍人、秘書丞。

translations.literal: He was made a student at the Imperial University, ranked high in the archery examination, was appointed Secretary, and was promoted to Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial University, ranked high in the archery examination, became Secretary, then Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Secretary.

sentences.zh: 轉宣城王文學、友、太子中庶子，掌管記。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Literary Adjunct, Companion, and Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent for the Prince of Xuancheng, and managed the records.
translations.idiomatic: He became literary adjunct and companion to the Prince of Xuancheng, Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and keeper of the records.

sentences.zh: 俄遷侍中，旣拜入見，高祖從容問何敬容曰：「褚彥回年幾爲宰相？

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Attendant Gentleman. When he had received appointment and entered for audience, the High Ancestor casually asked He Jingrong, "At what age did Chu Yanhui become chief minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Attendant Gentleman. On his first audience after appointment the High Ancestor casually asked He Jingrong, "At what age did Chu Yanhui become chief minister?"

sentences.zh: 」敬容對曰：「少過三十。

translations.literal: Jingrong replied, "A little past thirty."
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong answered, "A little past thirty."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「今之王訓，無謝彥回。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Today's Wang Xun is not inferior to Yanhui."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Today's Wang Xun is no less than Yanhui."

sentences.zh: 訓美容儀，善進止，文章之美，爲後進領袖。

translations.literal: Xun had a beautiful appearance and graceful bearing in advancing and withdrawing. The beauty of his writing made him the leader among the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was handsome and moved with grace; the elegance of his writing made him the leader of the younger generation.

sentences.zh: 在春宮特被恩禮。

translations.literal: In the Eastern Palace he was especially favored with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In the crown prince's palace he enjoyed special favor and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 以疾終於位，時年二十六。

translations.literal: He died of illness in office, aged twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office of illness at twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈本官。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his former office.
translations.idiomatic: His former rank was conferred on him posthumously.

sentences.zh: 諡溫子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Marquis Wen.

sentences.zh: 王泰字仲通，志長兄慈之子也。

translations.literal: Wang Tai, styled Zhongtong, was the son of Ci, the elder brother of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tai, whose style was Zhongtong, was the son of Ci, Zhi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 慈，齊時歷侍中、吳郡，知名在志右。

translations.literal: Ci, in the Qi period, served in succession as Attendant Gentleman and Administrator of Wu Commandery, and was famed beyond Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ci under Qi had served as Attendant Gentleman and Administrator of Wu Commandery and was even better known than Zhi.

sentences.zh: 泰幼敏悟，年數歲時，祖母集諸孫侄，散棗栗於床上，羣兒皆競之，泰獨不取。

translations.literal: Tai was clever and perceptive from childhood. When his grandmother gathered the grandsons and nephews and scattered dates and chestnuts on the bed, all the children scrambled for them, but Tai alone did not take any.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was quick-witted from childhood. Once his grandmother gathered the grandchildren, scattered dates and chestnuts on the bed, and every child snatched at them—Tai alone took none.

sentences.zh: 問其故，對曰：「不取，自當得賜。

translations.literal: Asked why, he replied, "If I do not take them, I shall receive them as gifts in due course."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "If I leave them, I will be given my share in due course."

sentences.zh: 」由是中表異之。

translations.literal: Because of this his cousins and in-laws were struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen and in-laws marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 旣長，通和溫雅，人不見其喜慍之色。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was mild and warm in manner, and people never saw joy or anger in his face.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was gentle and mild; no one ever saw joy or anger on his face.

sentences.zh: 起家爲著作郎，不拜，改除秘書郎，遷前將軍、法曹行參軍、司徒東閤祭酒、車騎主簿。

translations.literal: He began his career as Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat but did not accept the post. He was reassigned as Secretary, then promoted to Acting Gentleman in the Law Bureau of the General of the Vanguard, Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Sikong, and Chief Clerk to the General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered Attendant Gentleman in the Secretariat but declined, became Secretary, then rose through acting gentleman in the Vanguard's law bureau, libationer of the Sikong's Eastern Pavilion, and chief clerk to the General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 高祖霸府建，以泰爲驃騎功曹史。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor established his Chief Minister's headquarters, he made Tai Recorder in the office of the General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu opened his chief minister's headquarters, he made Tai recorder on the staff of the General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was promoted to Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian he was promoted to Secretary.

sentences.zh: 齊永元末，後宮火，延燒秘書，圖書散亂殆盡。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan of Qi, fire broke out in the rear palace and spread to the Secretariat; books and records were scattered and nearly all lost.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongyuan in Qi a fire in the rear palace spread to the Secretariat and books were scattered until nearly all were lost.

sentences.zh: 泰爲丞，表校定繕寫，高祖從之。

translations.literal: Tai as Secretary submitted a memorial requesting collation and copying, and the High Ancestor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: As Secretary Tai memorialized for collation and copying, and the High Ancestor agreed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出爲南徐州別駕從事史，居職有能名。

translations.literal: He went out as Assistant Administrator of Southern Xuzhou and distinguished himself in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as assistant administrator of Southern Xuzhou and won a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 復徵中書侍郎，敕掌吏部郎事。

translations.literal: He was summoned again as Vice Director of the Secretariat and ordered to handle the affairs of the Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Vice Director of the Secretariat and ordered to handle the vice minister of personnel's duties.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事黃門侍郎、員外散騎常侍，並掌吏部如故，俄卽真。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and Extraordinary Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, still handling the Ministry of Personnel as before, and soon received the substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates and Extraordinary Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, still managing personnel affairs, and soon held the substantive post.

sentences.zh: 自過江，吏部郎不復典大選，令史以下，小人求競者輻湊，前後少能稱職。

translations.literal: Since crossing the Yangtze, Vice Ministers of Personnel had no longer presided over great selection; clerks and below were besieged by petty men seeking advancement, and few before or after could fill the post worthily.
translations.idiomatic: Since the crossing south of the Yangtze, vice ministers of personnel had ceased to control major appointments; petty men crowded the clerks' offices, and few incumbents had been equal to the task.

sentences.zh: 泰爲之不通關求，吏先至者卽補，不爲貴賤請囑易意，天下稱平。

translations.literal: Tai would not open his gate to such requests; whoever arrived first was appointed, and he did not alter his judgment for pleas of the noble or humble. The realm called it fair.
translations.idiomatic: Tai refused such back-door traffic; the first petitioner through the gate received the post, and he did not bend for noble or humble pleaders. The empire called it fair.

sentences.zh: 累遷爲廷尉，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Minister of Justice and Left Chief Clerk of the Sikong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Justice and left chief clerk of the Sikong.

sentences.zh: 出爲明威將軍、新安太守，在郡和理得民心。

translations.literal: He went out as General of Bright Martial Power and Administrator of Xin'an, where his government was harmonious and orderly and he won the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as General of Bright Martial Power and Administrator of Xin'an, governing harmoniously and winning the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 徵爲寧遠將軍，安右長史，俄遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as General of Far Pacification and Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Right, and soon promoted to Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as General of Far Pacification and chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Right, then soon made Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 尋爲太子庶子、領步兵校尉，復爲侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he became Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Colonel of the Footsoldiers, then again Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Colonel of the Footsoldiers, then Attendant Gentleman again.

sentences.zh: 仍遷仁威長史、南蘭陵太守，行南康王府、州、國事。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Chief Clerk of Manifest Benevolence, Administrator of Nan Lanling, and acting administrator of the affairs of the Prince of Nankang's fief, commandery, and state.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk of Manifest Benevolence and Administrator of Nan Lanling, acting for the Prince of Nankang's fief, commandery, and state.

sentences.zh: 王遷職，復爲北中郎長史、行豫章王府、州、國事，太守如故。

translations.literal: When the prince was transferred, he again became Chief Clerk to the General of the North in the Center, acting for the Prince of Yuzhang's fief, commandery, and state, while remaining Administrator as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince moved on, he became chief clerk to the General of the North in the Center, acting for the Prince of Yuzhang's fief, commandery, and state, while keeping the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入爲都官尚書。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 泰能接人士，士多懷泰，每願其居選官。

translations.literal: Tai was able to win over gentlemen; many men cherished him and always hoped he would hold the post of selection.
translations.idiomatic: Tai knew how to draw men to him; many cherished him and longed to see him in charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 頃之，爲吏部尚書，衣冠屬望，未及選舉，仍疾，改除散騎常侍、左驍騎將軍，未拜，卒，時年四十五。

translations.literal: Before long he became Minister of Personnel, to whom the gentry looked with hope, but before he could conduct selection he fell ill. He was reassigned as Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Left Valiant Cavalry but did not accept and died, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Minister of Personnel, the office the gentry awaited, but fell ill before he could conduct a round of appointments. He was reassigned as Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Left Valiant Cavalry, accepted neither, and died at forty-five.

sentences.zh: 諡夷子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Marquis Yi.

sentences.zh: 初，泰無子，養兄子祁，晚有子廓。

translations.literal: At first Tai had no son and adopted his elder brother's son Qi; late in life he had a son Kuo.
translations.idiomatic: At first Tai had no son and adopted his brother's son Qi; late in life he fathered Kuo.

sentences.zh: 王份字季文，琅邪人也。

translations.literal: Wang Fen, styled Jiwen, was a man of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fen, whose style was Jiwen, came from Langya.

sentences.zh: 祖僧朗，宋開府儀同三司、元公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Senglang was Grand Master with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies and Duke Yuan of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Senglang had held credentials equal to the Three Excellencies as Duke Yuan of Song.

sentences.zh: 父粹，黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Cui was Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cui had been Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 份十四而孤，解褐車騎主簿。

translations.literal: Fen was orphaned at fourteen and began his career as Chief Clerk to the General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at fourteen, he entered service as chief clerk to the General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧遠將軍、始安內史。

translations.literal: He went out as General of Far Pacification and Administrator of Shian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as General of Far Pacification and Administrator of Shian.

sentences.zh: 袁粲之誅，親故無敢視者，份獨往致慟，由是顯名。

translations.literal: When Yuan Can was executed, none of his kin and friends dared to look upon him, but Fen alone went to express mourning and thereby became famous.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Can was executed, no friend or kinsman dared approach the body, but Fen alone went to mourn him and won renown.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中舍人，太尉屬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Aide in the Grand Commandant's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent and aide in the Grand Commandant's office.

sentences.zh: 出爲晉安內史。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎，轉大司農。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Secretariat and transferred to Minister of Grand Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Secretariat, then Minister of Grand Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 份兄奐於雍州被誅，奐子肅奔于魏，份自拘請罪，齊世祖知其誠款，喻而遣之。

translations.literal: Fen's elder brother Huan was executed in Yong Province; Huan's son Su fled to Wei. Fen bound himself and asked for punishment. Emperor Shizu of Qi knew his sincerity and explained the matter to him before sending him away.
translations.idiomatic: Fen's elder brother Huan was executed in Yong Province; Huan's son Su fled to Wei. Fen turned himself in to accept punishment. Emperor Shizu of Qi knew his sincerity, reassured him, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 屬肅屢引魏人來侵疆埸，世祖嘗因侍坐，從容謂份曰：「比有北信不？

translations.literal: As Su repeatedly led Wei troops to raid the borders, the Emperor once said to Fen while seated in attendance, "Have there been northern dispatches lately?"
translations.idiomatic: When Su repeatedly led Wei raiders against the frontier, the Emperor once asked Fen at leisure during attendance, "Any news from the north lately?"

sentences.zh: 」份斂容對曰：「肅旣近忘墳柏，寧遠憶有臣。

translations.literal: Fen composed his expression and replied, "Su has lately forgotten his ancestral graves; how could I, from afar, still regard him as a kinsman?"
translations.idiomatic: Fen composed himself and answered, "Su has already forgotten his ancestral graves; how could I, far away, still claim him as kin?"

sentences.zh: 」帝亦以此亮焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor also for this reason regarded him as bright.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor admired him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 尋除寧朔將軍、零陵內史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 徵爲黃門侍郎，以父終於此職，固辭不拜，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, but because his father had died in that post he firmly declined and would not accept, and was transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, but because his father had died in that office he firmly declined and was made Director of the Secretariat instead.

sentences.zh: 天監初，除散騎常侍、領步兵校尉、兼起部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was made Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Colonel of the Footsoldiers, and concurrently Minister for Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianjian he became Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Colonel of the Footsoldiers, and concurrent Minister for Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗於宴席問羣臣曰：「朕爲有爲無？

translations.literal: The High Ancestor once asked the assembled ministers at a banquet, "Am I one who acts, or not?"
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet the High Ancestor once asked the assembled ministers, "Am I a man of action or not?"

sentences.zh: 」份對曰：「陛下應萬物爲有，體至理爲無。

translations.literal: Fen replied, "Your Majesty responds to the myriad things as one who acts, yet embodies supreme principle as one who does not."
translations.idiomatic: Fen answered, "Your Majesty meets the myriad things as one who acts, yet embodies supreme principle as one who does not."

sentences.zh: 」高祖稱善。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor praised the reply.

sentences.zh: 出爲宣城太守，轉吳郡太守，遷寧朔將軍、北中郎豫章王長史、蘭陵太守，行南徐府州事。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xuancheng, transferred to Administrator of Wu Commandery, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North, Chief Clerk to the Prince of Yuzhang of the North in the Center, and Administrator of Lanling, acting for the affairs of Southern Xuzhou and its prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Xuancheng, then Wu Commandery, then became General Who Pacifies the North, chief clerk to Prince Yuzhang of the North in the Center, and Administrator of Lanling, acting for Southern Xuzhou and its prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 遷太常卿、太子右率、散騎常侍，侍東宮，除金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Ceremonies, Right Commander of the Heir Apparent's Guard, Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, attending the Eastern Palace, and was given the rank of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Ceremonies, right commander of the crown prince's guard, Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry attending the Eastern Palace, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 復爲智武將軍、南康王長史，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: He again became General of Manifest Martial Power and Chief Clerk to the Prince of Nankang, with salary of two thousand shi in the middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: He again became General of Manifest Martial Power and chief clerk to the Prince of Nankang, with salary of two thousand shi in the middle grade.

sentences.zh: 復入爲散騎常侍、金紫光祿、南徐州大中正，給親信二十人。

translations.literal: He entered the capital again as Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Chief Rectifier of Southern Xuzhou, with twenty personal attendants granted.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and chief rectifier of Southern Xuzhou, with twenty personal attendants granted.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，尋加侍中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and soon given the additional post of Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and soon given the additional post of Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時修建二郊，份以本官領大匠卿，遷散騎常侍、右光祿大夫，加親信爲四十人。

translations.literal: At that time the suburban altars were being built; Fen in his former office headed the office of the Grand Master Builder, was promoted to Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and his personal attendants were increased to forty.
translations.idiomatic: While the suburban altars were under construction, Fen in his former rank headed the Grand Master Builder's office, was promoted to Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and his personal attendants were doubled to forty.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、特進、左光祿，復以本官監丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Gentleman, Special Advance, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and again in his former office supervised the Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Attendant Gentleman, Special Advance, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and again supervised the Administrator of Danyang in his former capacity.

sentences.zh: 普通五年三月，卒，時年七十九。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year of Putong he died, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year of Putong he died, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 詔贈本官，賻錢四十萬，布四百匹，蠟四百斤，給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲。

translations.literal: An edict granted his former office; funeral gifts were forty thousand cash, four hundred bolts of cloth, and four hundred jin of wax. Eastern Garden secret implements were provided, one set of court robes, and one suit of garments.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted his former rank; funeral gifts were forty thousand cash, four hundred bolts of cloth, and four hundred jin of wax, with Eastern Garden ritual vessels, one set of court robes, and one suit of garments.

sentences.zh: 諡胡子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Marquis Hu.

sentences.zh: 長子琳，字孝璋，舉南徐州秀才，釋褐征虜建安王法曹、司徒東閤祭酒，南平王文學。

translations.literal: His eldest son Lin, styled Xiaozhang, was recommended as a provincial graduate of Southern Xuzhou, began his career as Acting Gentleman in the Law Bureau of the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Prince of Jian'an, Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Sikong, and Literary Adjunct to the Prince of Pingping.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Lin, styled Xiaozhang, was recommended as Southern Xuzhou's provincial graduate and entered service as acting gentleman in Prince Jian'an's law bureau, libationer of the Sikong's Eastern Pavilion, and literary adjunct to the Prince of Pingping.

sentences.zh: 尚義興公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Yixing and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Yixing and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎，衛軍謝朏長史，員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Chief Clerk to the General of the Guard Xie Tiao, and Extraordinary Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Secretariat, chief clerk to Xie Tiao, General of the Guard, and Extraordinary Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 出爲明威將軍、東陽太守，徵司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He went out as General of Bright Martial Power and Administrator of Dongyang, and was summoned as Left Chief Clerk of the Sikong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as General of Bright Martial Power and Administrator of Dongyang, then recalled as left chief clerk of the Sikong.

sentences.zh: 錫字公嘏，琳之第二子也。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Gongjia, was Lin's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, whose style was Gongjia, was Lin's second son.

sentences.zh: 幼而警悟，與兄弟受業，至應休散，常獨留不起。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and perceptive. He studied with his brothers, and when it came time to break for rest he alone would remain and not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from childhood, he studied with his brothers; when the class broke for rest he alone stayed seated.

sentences.zh: 年七八歲，猶隨公主入宮，高祖嘉其聰敏，常爲朝士說之。

translations.literal: At seven or eight years of age he still followed the princess into the palace. The High Ancestor praised his quick wit and often spoke of him to court officials.
translations.idiomatic: When he was seven or eight he still accompanied the princess into the palace. The High Ancestor admired his quick mind and often spoke of him to the court.

sentences.zh: 精力不倦，致損右目。

translations.literal: His energy never flagged, until it damaged his right eye.
translations.idiomatic: He never tired in his studies, until the strain cost him the sight of his right eye.

sentences.zh: 公主每節其業，爲飾居宇。

translations.literal: The princess often regulated his work and furnished his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The princess often kept his studies within bounds and saw to the furnishing of his rooms.

sentences.zh: 雖童稚之中，一無所好。

translations.literal: Even among children, he had no fondness for anything else.
translations.idiomatic: Even among children his age, he cared for nothing but his books.

sentences.zh: 十二，爲國子生。

translations.literal: At twelve he became a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 十四，舉清茂，除秘書郎，與范陽張伯緒齊名，俱爲太子舍人。

translations.literal: At fourteen he was recommended as Pure and Eminent, appointed Secretary Gentleman, and was as famous as Zhang Boqi of Fanyang; both became Attendants to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was nominated as Pure and Eminent, appointed Secretary Gentleman, and won a reputation equal to Zhang Boqi of Fanyang; both served as Attendants to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his father and observed the rites to the full.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he entered mourning and fulfilled every rite.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除太子洗馬。

translations.literal: When the mourning ended, he was appointed Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was made Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時昭明尚幼，未與臣僚相接。

translations.literal: At that time Zhaoming was still young and had not yet met with the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming was still a child then and had not yet been introduced to the officials.

sentences.zh: 高祖敕：「太子洗馬王錫、秘書郎張纘，親表英華，朝中髦俊，可以師友事之。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor ordered: "Groom of the Heir Apparent Wang Xi and Secretary Gentleman Zhang Zuan are close kin and outstanding talents, the finest young men at court—they may be treated as teachers and friends.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor commanded: "Groom of the Heir Apparent Wang Xi and Secretary Gentleman Zhang Zuan, kinsmen of shining talent and the court's foremost young worthies, should be treated as teachers and friends.

sentences.zh: 」以戚屬封永安侯，除晉安王友，稱疾不行，敕許受詔停都。

translations.literal: " By virtue of imperial kin he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yong'an and appointed Companion to the Prince of Jin'an, but pleaded illness and did not go; an edict permitted him to receive orders while remaining in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " As an imperial relative he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yong'an and appointed Companion to the Prince of Jin'an, but pleaded illness and declined; an edict allowed him to receive orders while staying in the capital.

sentences.zh: 王冠日，以府僚攝事。

translations.literal: On the day the prince came of age, he acted for the prince's staff in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince came of age, he handled the prince's staff duties in their stead.

sentences.zh: 普通初，魏始連和，使劉善明來聘，敕使中書舍人朱异接之，預宴者皆歸化北人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putong, Wei first made peace and sent Liu Shanming on a friendly mission. An edict had Palace Attendant Zhu Yi receive him; those at the banquet were all northerners who had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Putong, Wei newly made peace and sent Liu Shanming as envoy. The High Ancestor ordered Palace Attendant Zhu Yi to receive him; everyone at the banquet was a northerner who had surrendered to the south.

sentences.zh: 善明負其才氣，酒酣謂异曰：「南國辯學如中書者幾人？

translations.literal: Shanming relied on his talent and spirit; when the wine had gone to his head he said to Yi, "How many men of eloquent learning like the Palace Attendant are there in the Southern Realm?
translations.idiomatic: Shanming, confident in his wit, said once the wine had warmed him to Yi: "How many men in the south with your gift for debate and learning?

sentences.zh: 」异對曰：「异所以得接賓宴者，乃分職是司。

translations.literal: " Yi replied, "The reason I am able to attend this guest banquet is that receiving envoys is my assigned duty.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi answered: "I am here because receiving envoys is my assigned duty.

sentences.zh: 二國通和，所敦親好；

translations.literal: When two states are at peace, what we cultivate is cordial friendship;
translations.idiomatic: When two realms are at peace, what we cultivate is cordial friendship;

sentences.zh: 若以才辯相尚，則不容見使。

translations.literal: if one were to compete in talent and debate, then I would not be fit to be sent on such a mission."
translations.idiomatic: if we were to vie in wit and rhetoric, I would hardly be fit to serve as envoy."

sentences.zh: 」善明乃曰：「王錫、張纘，北間所聞，云何可見？

translations.literal: Shanming then said, "Wang Xi and Zhang Zuan are names heard of in the north—how might one see them?
translations.idiomatic: Shanming then asked: "Wang Xi and Zhang Zuan are names we have heard in the north—how might we meet them?

sentences.zh: 」异具啓，敕卽使於南苑設宴，錫與張纘、朱异四人而已。

translations.literal: " Yi reported in full; an edict immediately had a banquet set in the Southern Park—only Xi, Zhang Zuan, Zhu Yi, and four men in all.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi reported at once; an edict had a banquet prepared in the Southern Park with only Xi, Zhang Zuan, Zhu Yi, and the envoy—four men in all.

sentences.zh: 善明造席，遍論經史，兼以嘲謔，錫、纘隨方酬對，無所稽疑，未嘗訪彼一事，善明甚相歎挹。

translations.literal: Shanming came to the mat and discoursed broadly on the classics and histories, mixing in banter and jest. Xi and Zuan answered as occasion demanded, with nothing left in doubt; they never once had to ask him about a single matter. Shanming was deeply impressed and admiring.
translations.idiomatic: Shanming took his place and ranged through the classics and histories, seasoning his talk with wit and banter. Xi and Zuan met every topic as it came, never at a loss; they never once had to ask him a question. Shanming was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 佗日謂异曰：「一日見二賢，實副所期，不有君子，安能爲國！」

translations.literal: Another day he said to Yi, "In one day I have seen two worthies—it truly fulfills what I hoped. Without gentlemen such as these, how could a state endure!"
translations.idiomatic: On another day he told Yi: "In a single day I have met two true talents—it fulfills everything I hoped. Without men like these, how could any state stand?"

sentences.zh: 轉中書郎，遷給事黃門侍郎、尚書吏部郎中，時年二十四。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, promoted to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate and Director of the Personnel Bureau in the Masters of Writing, at the age of twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, then Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate and Director of the Personnel Bureau in the Masters of Writing, at twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 謂親友曰：「吾以外戚，謬被時知，多叨人爵，本非其志；

translations.literal: He told relatives and friends, "Because I am an imperial in-law I have wrongly been known to the age and have received many ranks beyond my desert—this was never my wish;
translations.idiomatic: He told kin and friends: "As an imperial in-law I have been wrongly singled out by the times and given many honors I do not deserve—never my wish;

sentences.zh: 兼比羸病，庶務難擁，安能舍其所好而徇所不能。

translations.literal: moreover I am lately frail and ill, and the multitude of affairs is hard to bear—how could I abandon what I love and pursue what I cannot do?
translations.idiomatic: and lately I am frail and ill, unable to bear the press of affairs—how could I abandon what I love to chase what I cannot do?

sentences.zh: 」乃稱疾不拜。

translations.literal: " He then pleaded illness and did not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " He pleaded illness and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 便謝遣胥徒，拒絕賓客，掩扉覃思，室宇蕭然。

translations.literal: He dismissed his clerks, turned away guests, shut his door and plunged into thought; his rooms were utterly bare.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed his clerks, refused visitors, shut his door and gave himself to study; his house was stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 中大通六年正月，卒，時年三十六。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Zhongdatong he died, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year of Zhongdatong he died, aged thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant; Eastern Garden secret implements were granted, one set of court robes, and one suit of garments.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant, with Eastern Garden ritual vessels, one set of court robes, and one suit of garments.

sentences.zh: 諡貞子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子泛、湜。

translations.literal: His sons were Fan and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Fan and Shi.

sentences.zh: 僉字公會，錫第五弟也。

translations.literal: Qian, styled Gonghui, was Xi's fifth younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, whose style was Gonghui, was Xi's fifth younger brother.

sentences.zh: 八歲丁父憂，哀毀過禮。

translations.literal: At eight he entered mourning for his father; his grief and emaciation exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he mourned his father; his grief and wasting exceeded what the rites required.

sentences.zh: 服闋，召補國子生，祭酒袁昂稱爲通理。

translations.literal: When the mourning ended he was summoned to fill a vacancy as a student of the Imperial Academy; Libationer Yuan Ang called him thoroughly versed in principle.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed a student of the Imperial Academy; Libationer Yuan Ang praised him as thoroughly versed in principle.

sentences.zh: 策高第，除長史兼秘書郎中，歷尚書殿中郎，太子中舍人，與吳郡陸襄對掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: He placed at the top in the examination, was appointed Chief Clerk with concurrent duty as Secretary Director, served as Director in the Palace Secretariat, Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and with Lu Xiang of Wu command jointly managed the Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the examination, became Chief Clerk and concurrent Secretary Director, served as Director in the Palace Secretariat and Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and with Lu Xiang of Wu jointly kept the Eastern Palace records.

sentences.zh: 出爲建安太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Administrator of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 山酋方善、謝稀聚徒依險，屢爲民患，僉潛設方略，率衆平之，有詔褒美，頒示州郡。

translations.literal: Mountain chiefs Fang Shan and Xie Xi gathered followers and relied on the terrain; they repeatedly harmed the people. Qian secretly devised a plan, led troops, and pacified them. An edict praised him and circulated the report through the provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain chiefs Fang Shan and Xie Xi had gathered bands in the hills and repeatedly preyed on the people. Qian laid secret plans, led troops, and crushed them. An edict commended him and sent the report through every province and commandery.

sentences.zh: 除武威將軍、始興內史，丁所生母憂，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Martial Prestige and Interior Minister of Shixing, but entered mourning for his birth mother and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of Martial Prestige and Interior Minister of Shixing, but when his birth mother died he firmly refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 又除寧遠將軍、南康內史，屬盧循作亂，復轉僉爲安成內史，以鎮撫之。

translations.literal: He was again appointed General of Pacifying the Distance and Interior Minister of Nankang; when Lu Xun rebelled, Qian was transferred to Interior Minister of Ancheng to pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made General of Pacifying the Distance and Interior Minister of Nankang; when Lu Xun rebelled, Qian was transferred to Interior Minister of Ancheng to restore order.

sentences.zh: 還除黃門侍郎，尋爲安西武陵王長史、蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate, and soon became Chief Clerk to Prince Wu of the West, General of Pacifying the West, and Administrator of Shu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court he became Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate, then Chief Clerk to Prince Wu of the West and Administrator of Shu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 僉憚岨嶮，固以疾辭，因以黜免。

translations.literal: Qian feared the steep and perilous route and firmly pleaded illness to decline; for this he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian dreaded the perilous mountain roads and pleaded illness; he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，除戎昭將軍、尚書左丞，復補黃門侍郎，遷太子中庶子，掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed General of Martial Brilliance and Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing, again restored as Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate, promoted to Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and managed the Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was made General of Martial Brilliance and Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing, restored as Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate, promoted Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and put in charge of the Eastern Palace records.

sentences.zh: 太清二年十二月，卒，時年四十五。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Taiqing he died, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Taiqing he died, aged forty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，給東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant; Eastern Garden secret implements were granted, one set of court robes, and one suit of garments.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant, with Eastern Garden ritual vessels, one set of court robes, and one suit of garments.

sentences.zh: 承聖三年，世祖追詔曰：「賢而不伐曰恭，諡恭子。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Chengsheng, Emperor Yuan issued a retrospective edict: "The worthy who does not boast is called Gong—his posthumous title is Marquis Gong."
