translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chengsheng, Emperor Yuan issued a retrospective edict: "The worthy who does not boast is called Gong"—and gave him the posthumous title Marquis Gong.

sentences.zh: 張充字延符，吳郡人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong, styled Yanfu, was a man of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong, whose style was Yanfu, came from Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父緒，齊特進、金紫光祿大夫，有名前代。

translations.literal: His father Xu was Special Advance of Qi and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, famous in the previous age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xu had been Special Advance under Qi and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, renowned in the previous dynasty.

sentences.zh: 充少時，不持操行，好逸遊。

translations.literal: In youth Chong did not keep to proper conduct and loved idle roaming.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Chong cared little for propriety and loved idle sport.

sentences.zh: 緒嘗請假還吳，始入西郭，值充出獵，左手臂鷹，右手牽狗，遇緒船至，便放絏脫镡，拜於水次。

translations.literal: Xu once asked leave to return to Wu; just as he entered the western suburb, he met Chong going out to hunt—hawk on his left arm, hound in his right hand. When Xu's boat arrived, Chong at once loosed hawk and hound and bowed at the water's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Xu once took leave to return to Wu. At the western gate he met Chong setting out to hunt, hawk on his left arm and hound in his right hand. When Xu's boat drew near, Chong released hawk and hound and bowed from the shore.

sentences.zh: 緒曰：「一身兩役，無乃勞乎？

translations.literal: Xu said, "One body, two tasks—is it not exhausting?
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "One body serving two masters—is that not exhausting?

sentences.zh: 」充跪對曰：「充聞三十而立，今二十九矣，請至來歲而敬易之。

translations.literal: " Chong knelt and replied, "Chong has heard that at thirty one stands firm; I am twenty-nine now—please let me wait until next year and then respectfully change."
translations.idiomatic: " Chong knelt and answered: "I have heard that at thirty a man stands firm; I am twenty-nine—let me wait until next year and then mend my ways."

sentences.zh: 」緒曰：「過而能改，顏氏子有焉。

translations.literal: Xu said, "To err and then reform—such was the son of the Yan clan."
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "To err and then reform—there was such a man in the house of Yan."

sentences.zh: 」及明年，便修身改節。

translations.literal: The next year he indeed cultivated himself and changed his ways.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he truly reformed himself.

sentences.zh: 學不盈載，多所該覽，尤明《老》、《易》，能清言，與從叔稷俱有令譽。

translations.literal: Though his formal study had not filled a year, he had read widely in many fields, was especially versed in the Laozi and Changes, could hold pure discourse, and with his younger cousin of the same clan, Ji, both enjoyed a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had studied formally for less than a year, he had read widely, was especially versed in the Laozi and the Changes, could hold pure discourse, and with his cousin Ji shared a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 起家撫軍行參軍，遷太子舍人、尚書殿中郎、武陵王友。

translations.literal: He began his career as Acting Aide on the Pacifying Army staff, was transferred to Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Director in the Palace Secretariat, and Companion to the Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as acting aide on the Pacifying Army staff, then Attendant to the Heir Apparent, Director in the Palace Secretariat, and Companion to the Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令王儉當朝用事，武帝皆取決焉。

translations.literal: At that time Chief Minister Wang Jian held power in court, and Emperor Wu took all decisions through him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Jian as Chief Minister held the reins of government, and Emperor Wu deferred to him in every decision.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘗欲以充父緒爲尚書僕射，訪於儉，儉對曰：「張緒少有清望，誠美選也；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu once wished to appoint Chong's father Xu as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and consulted Jian. Jian replied, "Zhang Xu from youth has had a pure reputation—he is indeed a fine choice;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once wished to make Chong's father Xu Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and asked Jian's view. Jian answered: "Zhang Xu has enjoyed a spotless name since youth—a fine choice indeed;

sentences.zh: 然東士比無所執，緒諸子又多薄行，臣謂此宜詳擇。

translations.literal: yet among eastern gentlemen none in his line has held office, and Xu's sons are mostly of loose conduct—I say this merits careful selection."
translations.idiomatic: yet no one in his eastern clan has held high office, and his sons are mostly of loose conduct—I think this calls for careful scrutiny."

sentences.zh: 」帝遂止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 先是充兄弟皆輕俠，充少時又不護細行，故儉言之。

translations.literal: Earlier Chong's brothers had all been frivolous and reckless; in youth Chong too had not guarded small conduct—hence Jian's words.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's brothers had all been frivolous, and in youth Chong too had neglected propriety—hence Jian's remark.

sentences.zh: 充聞而慍，因與儉書曰：

translations.literal: Chong heard of it and was angry; he therefore wrote to Jian, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chong heard of it and took offense; he wrote to Jian:

sentences.zh: 吳國男子張充致書于琅邪王君侯侍者：頃日路長，愁霖韜晦，涼暑未平，想無虧攝。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong, a man of Wu, sends this letter to the attendants of the Marquis of Langya: The road has lately been long, melancholy rains have hidden the light, coolness and heat are not yet settled—I trust you have not suffered in health.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong of Wu to the attendants of the Marquis of Langya: The journey has been long of late, melancholy rains have veiled the sky, and the season's heat and chill are not yet settled—I trust you remain in good health.

sentences.zh: 充幸以魚釣之閑，鐮采之暇，時復以卷軸自娛，逍遙前史。

translations.literal: Chong has been fortunate, in the intervals of fishing and in the leisure of gathering firewood, sometimes to amuse himself with scrolls and roam freely through the histories of old.
translations.idiomatic: In the intervals of fishing and the leisure of gathering firewood, I have sometimes turned to my scrolls for pleasure and wandered freely through the histories of old.

sentences.zh: 從橫萬古，動默之路多端；

translations.literal: Stretching across ten thousand ages, the paths of action and stillness are many;
translations.idiomatic: Across ten thousand ages the paths of action and stillness branch in many directions;

sentences.zh: 紛綸百年，昇降之途不一。

translations.literal: tangled through a hundred years, the roads of ascent and descent are not one.
translations.idiomatic: through a hundred tangled years the roads of rise and fall are not one.

sentences.zh: 故以圓行方止，器之異也；

translations.literal: Hence the round travels and the square stops—the vessels differ;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the wheel rolls while the square rests—vessels differ;

sentences.zh: 金剛水柔，性之別也。

translations.literal: metal is hard and water is soft—the natures are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: metal is hard and water is soft—natures are not the same.

sentences.zh: 善御性者，不違金水之質；

translations.literal: One who skillfully governs nature does not violate the substance of metal and water;
translations.idiomatic: He who skillfully governs his nature does not violate the substance of metal and water;

sentences.zh: 善爲器者，不易方圓之用。

translations.literal: one who skillfully makes vessels does not alter the uses of square and round.
translations.idiomatic: he who skillfully shapes vessels does not alter the uses of square and round.

sentences.zh: 所以北海掛簪帶之高，河南降璽書之貴。

translations.literal: Hence Bei Hai hung up his cap and sash in high disdain, and He Nan received the preciousness of an imperial letter sent down.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Guo Tai of Bei Hai hung up cap and sash in lofty disdain, and Huangfu Mi of He Nan received the honor of an imperial letter sent down.

sentences.zh: 充生平少偶，不以利欲干懷，三十六年，差得以棲貧自澹。

translations.literal: All my life I have rarely found a match; profit and desire have never touched my breast. For thirty-six years I have been able, more or less, to dwell in poverty and keep myself calm.
translations.idiomatic: All my life I have rarely found my equal; profit and desire have never touched my heart. For thirty-six years I have dwelt in poverty and kept myself at peace.

sentences.zh: 介然之志，峭聳霜崖；

translations.literal: My solitary resolve rises steep as a frost-clad cliff;
translations.idiomatic: My solitary resolve rises sheer as a frost-white cliff;

sentences.zh: 確乎之情，峰橫海岸。

translations.literal: my firm intent stands peak upon peak along the seacoast.
translations.idiomatic: my firm intent stands like peaks ranged along the shore.

sentences.zh: 彯纓天閣，旣謝廊廟之華；

translations.literal: Tassels at the Gate of Heaven—I have already declined the glory of hall and temple;
translations.idiomatic: Court tassels at the Gate of Heaven—I have already declined the glory of hall and temple;

sentences.zh: 綴組雲臺，終慚衣冠之秀。

translations.literal: silken cords on the Cloud Terrace—I would always be shamed before the elegance of official dress.
translations.idiomatic: silken cords on the Cloud Terrace—I would always fall short before the elegance of official dress.

sentences.zh: 所以擯跡江皋，陽狂隴畔者，實由氣岸疏凝，情塗狷隔。

translations.literal: The reason I have cast aside my tracks on the river isles and feigned madness on the upland paths is truly that my spirit stands aloof and my feelings keep a narrow distance from the world.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I have hidden my tracks on the river isles and played the madman on the upland paths is that my spirit stands aloof and my heart keeps its distance from the world.

sentences.zh: 獨師懷抱，不見許於俗人；

translations.literal: Alone I hold to my inner truth, and the vulgar do not approve;
translations.idiomatic: Alone I hold to my inner truth, and the vulgar world does not approve;

sentences.zh: 孤秀神崖，每邅回於在世。

translations.literal: solitary and splendid on spirit's cliff, I am ever turned back while still in the world.
translations.idiomatic: solitary and splendid on spirit's cliff, I am ever turned back though still among the living.

sentences.zh: 故君山直上，蹙壓於當年；

translations.literal: Hence Junshan went straight upward and was crushed underfoot in his own day;
translations.idiomatic: Hence Yuan Yi of Junshan went straight upward and was crushed underfoot in his own day;

sentences.zh: 叔陽夐舉，晳甚晳稟乎千載。

translations.literal: Shuyang raised himself far off—clear and radiant, inheriting across a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hong of Shuyang raised himself far off—clear and radiant, shining across a thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 充所以長羣魚鳥，畢影松阿。

translations.literal: Therefore I have long kept company with fish and birds and cast my shadow wholly on pine-covered slopes.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have long kept company with fish and birds and cast my shadow wholly on pine-covered slopes.

sentences.zh: 半頃之田，足以輸稅；

translations.literal: Half a qing of fields is enough to pay the tax;
translations.idiomatic: Half a qing of fields suffices to pay the tax;

sentences.zh: 五畝之宅，樹以桑麻。

translations.literal: a five-mu homestead is planted with mulberry and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: a five-mu homestead is planted with mulberry and hemp.

sentences.zh: 嘯歌於川澤之間，諷味於澠池之上，氾濫於漁父之游，偃息於卜居之下。

translations.literal: I sing freely between river and marsh, savor verse on the banks above the Sheng Pool, drift in the fisherman's wanderings, and rest in the shade beneath the diviner's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: I sing freely between river and marsh, savor verse on the banks above the Sheng Pool, drift as the fisherman's wanderings, and rest beneath the diviner's dwelling.

sentences.zh: 如此而已，充何謝焉。

translations.literal: That is all—what has Chong to regret?
translations.idiomatic: That is all—what have I to regret?

sentences.zh: 若夫驚岩罩日，壯海逢天；

translations.literal: As for cliffs that startle and hood the sun, seas vast enough to meet the sky;
translations.idiomatic: As for cliffs that startle and hood the sun, seas vast enough to meet the sky;

sentences.zh: 竦石崩尋，分危落仞。

translations.literal: towering stones collapsing by the span, peaks split and perilous, falling sheer for a thousand ren—
translations.idiomatic: towering stones collapsing by the span, peaks split and perilous, falling sheer for a thousand ren—

sentences.zh: 桂蘭綺靡，叢雜於山幽；

translations.literal: cassia and orchid exquisite and dense, mingling in mountain depths;
translations.idiomatic: cassia and orchid exquisite and dense, mingling in mountain depths;

sentences.zh: 松柏森陰，相繚于澗曲。

translations.literal: pine and cypress casting deep shade, winding together in the crook of the stream.
translations.idiomatic: pine and cypress casting deep shade, winding together in the crook of the stream.

sentences.zh: 元卿於是乎不歸，伯休亦以茲長往。

translations.literal: It was for this that Yuanqing did not return, and Boxiu likewise departed forever on this account.
translations.idiomatic: For such scenes Yuanqing never returned, and Boxiu likewise departed forever.

sentences.zh: 若乃飛竿釣渚，濯足滄洲；

translations.literal: As for casting rods to fish on the islet, washing feet on the Cang Isle;
translations.idiomatic: As for casting rods to fish on the islet, washing feet on the Cang Isle;

sentences.zh: 獨浪煙霞，高臥風月。

translations.literal: alone upon the mist and glow, sleeping high in wind and moon.
translations.idiomatic: alone upon mist and glow, sleeping high in wind and moon.

sentences.zh: 悠悠琴酒，岫遠誰來？

translations.literal: Leisurely zither and wine—who comes from the distant peaks?
translations.idiomatic: Leisurely zither and wine—who comes from the distant peaks?

sentences.zh: 灼灼文談，空罷方寸。

translations.literal: Bright discourse alone—empty within the square inch.
translations.idiomatic: Bright discourse alone—empty within the square inch of the heart.

sentences.zh: 不覺鬰然千里，路阻江川。

translations.literal: Before I knew it, a thousand li of longing lay between us, the road blocked by river and pass.
translations.idiomatic: Before I knew it, a thousand li of longing lay between us, the road blocked by river and pass.

sentences.zh: 每至西風，何嘗不眷？

translations.literal: Whenever the west wind rises, how could I not yearn?
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the west wind rises, how could I not yearn?

sentences.zh: 聊因疾隙，略舉諸襟；

translations.literal: I take this interval of illness briefly to lay open what is in my breast;
translations.idiomatic: In this interval of illness I briefly lay open what is in my breast;

sentences.zh: 持此片言，輕枉高聽。

translations.literal: with these few words I lightly presume upon your lofty attention.
translations.idiomatic: with these few words I lightly presume upon your lofty attention.

sentences.zh: 丈人歲路未強，學優而仕；

translations.literal: You, sir, are not yet far from the prime of life; your learning is excellent and you have entered office;
translations.idiomatic: You, sir, are not yet far from your prime; your learning is excellent and you have entered office;

sentences.zh: 道佐蒼生，功橫海望。

translations.literal: your Way assists the common people, your merit spans the sea and your fame the horizon.
translations.idiomatic: your Way assists the common people, your merit spans the sea and your fame the horizon.

sentences.zh: 入朝則協長倩之誠，出議則抗仲子之節。

translations.literal: In entering court you match Changqian's sincerity; in going forth to debate you uphold Zhongzi's integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In court you match Changqian's sincerity; in debate you uphold Zhongzi's integrity.

sentences.zh: 可謂盛德維時，孤松獨秀者也。

translations.literal: One may call him a man of towering virtue suited to the age—a lone pine standing in peerless splendor.
translations.idiomatic: He may be called a man of towering virtue for his time—a lone pine standing in peerless splendor.

sentences.zh: 素履未詳，斯旅尚眇。

translations.literal: His plain conduct is not yet fully known, and this journey is still far.
translations.idiomatic: His unadorned way in life is not yet fully known, and the road before him still stretches far.

sentences.zh: 茂陵之彥，望冠蓋而長懷；

translations.literal: Men of talent at Maoling gaze upon passing carriages and long hold them in memory;
translations.idiomatic: The worthies of Maoling watch for your carriage and cherish you from afar;

sentences.zh: 霸山之氓，佇衣車而聳歎。

translations.literal: the folk of Bashan stand awaiting your robe and carriage and sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: the people of Bashan stand waiting for your passing train and sigh in wonder.

sentences.zh: 得無惜乎？

translations.literal: Does it not give cause for regret?
translations.idiomatic: Is that not a thing to regret?

sentences.zh: 若鴻裝撰御，鶴駕軒空，則岸不辭枯，山被其潤。

translations.literal: If you donned swan robes and took the crane carriage, leaving your chariot empty—then banks would not refuse to wither, and mountains would receive your moistening grace.
translations.idiomatic: If you donned swan robes and rode the crane carriage, leaving your chariot empty behind—then even withered banks would not refuse you, and the hills would drink your blessing.

sentences.zh: 奇禽異羽，或巖際而逢迎；

translations.literal: Strange birds of rare plumage would meet you at the cliff's edge;
translations.idiomatic: Strange birds in rare plumage would greet you at the cliff's edge;

sentences.zh: 弱霧輕煙，乍林端而奄藹。

translations.literal: light mist and thin smoke would suddenly veil the treetops.
translations.idiomatic: light mist and thin smoke would suddenly gather over the treetops.

sentences.zh: 東都不足奇，南山豈爲貴。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital would no longer seem marvelous, and the Southern Mountains would scarcely be prized.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital would lose its wonder, and the Southern Mountains would no longer seem so grand.

sentences.zh: 充昆西之百姓，岱表之一民。

translations.literal: Chong is but a common man west of Kun, a single subject on the slopes of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: I, Chong, am only a common man west of Kun, one subject among the foothills of Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 蠶而衣，耕且食，不能事王侯，覓知己，造時人，騁遊說，蓬轉于屠博之間，其歡甚矣。

translations.literal: I raise silkworms for clothing and plow for food; I cannot serve lords and princes, seek out confidants, court the men of the age, or roam among butchers and gamblers spreading persuasions—yet my joy in this is very great.
translations.idiomatic: I raise silkworms for my clothes and plow for my food. I cannot wait on lords, hunt for patrons, court the great men of the day, or wander among butchers and gamblers plying persuasion—yet in this I find great contentment.

sentences.zh: 丈人早遇承華，中逢崇禮。

translations.literal: You, sir, early met Chenghua and midway received Chongli.
translations.idiomatic: You, sir, were early received at Chenghua and midway honored at Chongli.

sentences.zh: 肆上之眷，望溢於早辰；

translations.literal: Imperial favor at court overflowed from the first light of morning;
translations.idiomatic: Favor at court overflowed from the first light of morning;

sentences.zh: 鄉下之言，謬延於造次。

translations.literal: rustic talk wrongly spread in haste.
translations.idiomatic: rustic gossip spread in haste and error.

sentences.zh: 然舉世皆謂充爲狂，充亦何能與諸君道之哉？

translations.literal: Yet the whole world calls Chong mad—how could Chong explain this to you gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the whole world calls me mad—how could I make any of you understand?

sentences.zh: 是以披聞見，掃心胸，述平生，論語默，所以通夢交魂，推衿送抱者，其惟丈人而已。

translations.literal: Therefore I lay open what I have seen and heard, sweep clear what is in my breast, recount my life, and speak of silence and speech—to join soul with soul in dream, to offer my collar and embrace: this I do for you alone, sir.
translations.idiomatic: So I lay open what I have seen and heard, sweep clear my heart, recount my life, and speak of silence and speech—to meet soul with soul in dream, to offer my collar and my embrace: this I do for you alone, sir.

sentences.zh: 關山夐隔，書罷莫因，儻遇樵者，妄塵執事。

translations.literal: Mountains and passes stand far apart; when this letter ends there is no further means to send it. If by chance you meet a woodcutter, pray let him carry it to your desk.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains and passes lie far between us; when this letter ends I have no other way to reach you. If you should meet a woodcutter by chance, pray let him bear it to your desk.

sentences.zh: 儉言之武帝，免充官，廢處久之。

translations.literal: Jian spoke of this to Emperor Wu; Chong was dismissed from office and lived in disgrace for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Jian reported the matter to Emperor Wu; Chong was stripped of office and lived in disgrace for a long while.

sentences.zh: 後爲司徒諮議參軍，與琅邪王思遠、同郡陸慧曉等，並爲司徒竟陵王賓客。

translations.literal: Later he became Consulting Adjutant to the Minister of Works, and together with Wang Siyuan of Langya, Lu Huixiao of the same commandery, and others, served as retainers to the Prince of Jingling, Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Consulting Adjutant to the Minister of Works and, with Wang Siyuan of Langya, Lu Huixiao of the same commandery, and others, served as retainers to the Minister of Works, Prince of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 入爲中書侍郎，尋轉給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Director of the Secretariat, and soon transferred to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Vice Director of the Secretariat and soon became Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 明帝作相，以充爲鎮軍長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming served as chief minister, he made Chong Chief Clerk to the General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Ming held the chief ministry, he appointed Chong chief clerk to the General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 出爲義興太守，爲政清靜，民吏便之。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Yixing; his government was pure and quiet, and officials and people alike found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Administrator of Yixing and governed with pure, quiet restraint; officials and common people alike were well served.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去職，服闋，除太子中庶子，遷侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he left office on account of his mother's mourning; when the mourning ended he was appointed Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned to mourn his mother; when mourning ended he was made Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and then Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 義師近次，東昏召百官入宮省，朝士慮禍，或往來酣宴，充獨居侍中省，不出閣。

translations.literal: When the army of righteousness drew near, Emperor Donghun summoned the hundred officials into the palace precinct. Court gentlemen feared disaster; some passed back and forth in drunken feasting, but Chong alone remained in the Attendant-in-Ordinary's office and did not leave his chamber.
translations.idiomatic: As the army of righteousness approached, Emperor Donghun summoned every official into the palace. Courtiers feared calamity; some shuttled between drunken banquets, but Chong alone stayed in the Attendant-in-Ordinary's office and never left his chamber.

sentences.zh: 城內旣害東昏，百官集西鐘下，召充不至。

translations.literal: Once Donghun had been killed within the city, the hundred officials assembled beneath the Western Bell Tower; Chong was summoned but did not come.
translations.idiomatic: After Donghun was killed inside the city, the hundred officials gathered beneath the Western Bell Tower; Chong was summoned but did not appear.

sentences.zh: 高祖霸府開，以充爲大司馬諮議參軍，遷梁王國郎中令、祠部尚書、領屯騎校尉，轉冠軍將軍、司徒左長史。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor opened his chief minister's headquarters, he made Chong Consulting Adjutant in the Chief Minister's office, promoted him to Director of the Liang King's Household, Minister of Rites, and Colonel of the Household Cavalry, then transferred him to General Who Vanquishes the Enemy and Left Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor opened his chief minister's headquarters, he appointed Chong Consulting Adjutant, then Director of the Liang King's Household, Minister of Rites, and Colonel of the Household Cavalry, and later General Who Vanquishes the Enemy and left chief clerk to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 天監初，除大常卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian he was made Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 尋遷吏部尚書，居選稱爲平允。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Personnel, and in office over selections he was praised as fair and even-handed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Minister of Personnel, where his handling of appointments won praise for fairness.

sentences.zh: 俄爲散騎常侍、雲騎將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he became Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Cloud Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of the Cloud Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋除晉陵太守，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Administrator of Jinling, with rank of two thousand shi within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Administrator of Jinling at the rank of two thousand shi within the palace.

sentences.zh: 徵拜散騎常侍、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 充長於義理，登堂講說，皇太子以下皆至。

translations.literal: Chong excelled in moral principle; when he ascended the hall to lecture, the Crown Prince and all below came to hear him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong excelled in moral principle; when he lectured from the hall, the Crown Prince and all ranks below attended.

sentences.zh: 時王侯多在學，執經以拜，充朝服而立，不敢當也。

translations.literal: At that time many princes were studying at the academy; holding the classics, they bowed to him, but Chong stood in court dress and did not dare accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Many princes were then studying at the academy; holding the classics, they bowed to him, but Chong stood in court dress and would not accept such deference.

sentences.zh: 轉左衛將軍，祭酒如故。

translations.literal: He transferred to General of the Left Guard while continuing as Director of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Left Guard while retaining the directorship of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 入爲尚書僕射，頃之，除雲麾將軍、吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; before long he was appointed General of the Cloud Banner and Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and soon became General of the Cloud Banner and Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 下車恤貧老，故舊莫不欣悅。

translations.literal: On taking office he cared for the poor and aged, and old friends all rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he cared for the poor and the aged, and every old friend rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 以疾自陳，徵爲散騎常侍，金紫光祿大夫，未及還朝，十三年，卒于吳，時年六十六。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and was summoned back as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; before he could return to court, in the thirteenth year he died in Wu at the age of sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and was recalled as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; before he could return to court he died in Wu in the thirteenth year, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 詔贈侍中、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 諡穆子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Mu.

sentences.zh: 子最嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zui succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zui succeeded to his line.

sentences.zh: 柳惲字文暢，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yun, styled Wenchang, was a man of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun, whose style was Wenchang, came from Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 少有志行，好學，善尺牘。

translations.literal: In youth he had ambition and conduct, loved learning, and was skilled at letters.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was ambitious and upright, loved learning, and wrote an elegant hand.

sentences.zh: 與陳郡謝瀹鄰居，瀹深所友愛。

translations.literal: He was a neighbor of Xie Yue of Chen Commandery, and Yue deeply befriended and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived next to Xie Yue of Chen Commandery, who deeply befriended and cherished him.

sentences.zh: 初，宋世有嵇元榮、羊蓋，並善彈琴，云傳戴安道之法，惲幼從之學，特窮其妙。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Song dynasty, Ji Yuanrong and Yang Gai were both skilled at the zither, claiming to transmit the method of Dai Andao. Yun studied with them from childhood and thoroughly mastered their subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: In the Song era Ji Yuanrong and Yang Gai had both been masters of the zither, claiming to transmit Dai Andao's method. Yun studied with them from childhood and mastered their art to its depths.

sentences.zh: 齊竟陵王聞而引之，以爲法曹行參軍，雅被賞狎。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingling of Qi heard of him and summoned him, appointing him Acting Adjutant in the Law Bureau; he was greatly favored and treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Qi’s Prince of Jingling heard of him and summoned him, making him Acting Adjutant in the Law Bureau; he was greatly favored and treated with warm intimacy.

sentences.zh: 王嘗置酒後園，有晉相謝安鳴琴在側，以授惲，惲彈爲雅弄。

translations.literal: The prince once set wine in the rear garden; a zither once played by the Jin minister Xie An stood at hand, and he gave it to Yun. Yun played an elegant piece.
translations.idiomatic: The prince once held wine in the rear garden; a zither that the Jin minister Xie An had once played stood nearby, and he handed it to Yun. Yun played an elegant air.

sentences.zh: 子良曰：「卿巧越嵇心，妙臻羊體，良質美手，信在今辰。

translations.literal: Ziliang said, "Your skill surpasses Ji's heart and reaches Yang's body; fine wood and beautiful hands—truly they meet in this moment.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang said, "Your art surpasses Ji's spirit and attains Yang's touch; fine timber and beautiful hands—truly they meet in you today.

sentences.zh: 豈止當世稱奇，足可追蹤古烈。

translations.literal: This is not merely marvel enough for the age; it can fully trace the great masters of old.
translations.idiomatic: This is not merely wonder enough for our age; it can fully match the great masters of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 」累遷太子洗馬，父憂去官。

translations.literal: " He was promoted in succession to Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household and left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: " He rose in succession to Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household, then left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，試守鄱陽相，聽吏屬，得盡三年喪禮，署之文教，百姓稱焉。

translations.literal: When the mourning ended he served on probation as Administrator of Poyang; he allowed his clerks and subordinates to observe the full three years of mourning rites, and in his written orders on culture and education the people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he served provisionally as Administrator of Poyang; he let his clerks and subordinates complete the full three years of mourning, and in his orders on culture and education the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 還除驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary on the staff of the General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary on the staff of the General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 惲立行貞素，以貴公子早有令名，少工篇什。

translations.literal: Yun's conduct was upright and plain; though a nobleman's son, he had early won a fine reputation and from youth was skilled at verse.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's bearing was upright and plain; though born a nobleman's son, he had early won a fine name and from youth wrote accomplished verse.

sentences.zh: 始爲詩曰：「亭皋本葉下，隴首秋雲飛。

translations.literal: He first composed a poem saying, "On the marshy bank the leaves fall from their stems; on Longshou the autumn clouds fly.
translations.idiomatic: His first poem ran: "On the marshy bank the leaves fall from their stems; on Longshou the autumn clouds fly.

sentences.zh: 」琅邪王元長見而嗟賞，因書齋壁。

translations.literal: " Wang Yuanchang of Langya saw it and sighed in admiration, and copied it onto his study wall.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Yuanchang of Langya read it and sighed in admiration, then copied it onto his study wall.

sentences.zh: 至是預曲宴，必被詔賦詩。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever he attended a private banquet, he was always commanded to compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever he attended an intimate banquet, he was always commanded to compose a poem.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉和高祖《登景陽樓》中篇云：「太液滄波起，長楊高樹秋。

translations.literal: He once composed in response to the High Ancestor's middle section of "Ascending the Jingyang Tower," saying, "Great Liquid's green waves rise; the tall poplars' high trees turn autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He once answered the High Ancestor's middle section of "Ascending the Jingyang Tower": "Great Liquid's green waves rise; the tall poplars' high boughs turn autumn.

sentences.zh: 翠華承漢遠，雕輦逐風遊。

translations.literal: The imperial splendor reaches far beyond Han; the carved carriage pursues the wind in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial splendor reaches far beyond Han; the carved carriage hunts the wind in flight.

sentences.zh: 」深爲高祖所美。

translations.literal: " The High Ancestor greatly admired it.
translations.idiomatic: " The High Ancestor greatly admired it.

sentences.zh: 當時咸共稱傳。

translations.literal: At the time all together praised and circulated it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time everyone praised and circulated it.

sentences.zh: 惲善奕朞，帝每敕侍坐，仍令定朞譜，第其優劣。

translations.literal: Yun was skilled at chess; the Emperor often ordered him to sit in attendance and had him compile a ranking of players and grade their relative merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was skilled at chess; the Emperor often had him sit in attendance and ordered him to compile a ranking of players and grade their relative strength.

sentences.zh: 二年，出爲吳興太守。

translations.literal: In the second year he went out as Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was posted as Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 六年。

translations.literal: The sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year,

sentences.zh: 徵爲散騎常侍，遷左民尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and transferred to Minister of the Left for the People.
translations.idiomatic: he was recalled as Attendant-in-Ordinary and transferred to Minister of the Left for the People.

sentences.zh: 八年，除持節、都督廣交桂越四州諸軍事、仁武將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief over the military affairs of the four provinces of Guang, Jiao, Gui, and Yue, General of Benevolent Martiality, General Who Pacifies the Yue as Central Commander, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Guang, Jiao, Gui, and Yue, General of Benevolent Martiality, General Who Pacifies the Yue as Central Commander, and Inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 徵爲秘書監，領左軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director of the Secretariat while also holding the post of General of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Director of the Secretariat and also held the post of General of the Left Army.

sentences.zh: 復爲吳興太守六年，爲政清靜，民吏懷之。

translations.literal: He again served six years as Administrator of Wuxing; his government was pure and quiet, and officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He served again as Administrator of Wuxing for six years; his government was pure and quiet, and officials and people cherished him.

sentences.zh: 於郡感疾，自陳解任，父老千餘人拜表陳請，事未施行。

translations.literal: While in the commandery he fell ill, pleaded to resign his post, and more than a thousand elders submitted a memorial begging him to remain; the matter had not yet been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: While in the commandery he fell ill and asked to resign; more than a thousand elders submitted a memorial begging him to stay, but the matter had not yet been decided.

sentences.zh: 天監十六年，卒，時年五十三。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Tianjian he died at the age of fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Tianjian he died, aged fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、中護軍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary and Central Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Central Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 惲旣善琴，嘗以今聲轉棄古法，乃著《清調論》，具有條流。

translations.literal: Since Yun was skilled at the zither, and having once transformed present-day sounds and abandoned the ancient method, he wrote "On Pure Tones," setting forth the rules in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was skilled at the zither; having once adapted present-day sounds and set aside the ancient method, he wrote "On Pure Tones," laying out the rules in full detail.

sentences.zh: 少子偃，字彥遊。

translations.literal: His youngest son Yan, styled Yanyou.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Yan, whose style was Yanyou.

sentences.zh: 年十二引見。

translations.literal: At twelve he was summoned for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he was summoned for an audience.

sentences.zh: 詔問讀何書，對曰《尚書》。

translations.literal: An edict asked what book he was reading; he answered, the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked what book he was reading; he answered, the Documents.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「有何美句？

translations.literal: He further asked, "What fine lines does it contain?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked again, "What fine lines does it hold?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「德惟善政，政在養民。

translations.literal: " He answered, "Virtue lies in good government, and good government lies in nourishing the people.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Virtue lies in good government, and good government lies in nourishing the people.

sentences.zh: 」衆咸異之。

translations.literal: " The assembly all marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: " The whole assembly marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 詔尚長城公主，拜駙馬都尉，都亭侯，太子舍人，洗馬，廬陵、鄱陽內史。

translations.literal: An edict had him marry the Princess of Changcheng; he was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, Marquis of Duting, Gentleman of the Heir Apparent's Household, Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household, and Internal Administrator of Luling and Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had him marry the Princess of Changcheng; he was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, Marquis of Duting, Gentleman of the Heir Apparent's Household, Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household, and Internal Administrator of Luling and Poyang.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dabao he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dabao he died.

sentences.zh: 蔡撙字景節，濟陽考城人。

translations.literal: Cai Zun, styled Jingjie, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zun, whose style was Jingjie, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 父興宗，宋左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，有重名前代。

translations.literal: His father Xingzong was Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Master of the Palace with the Staff of Three Divisions under Song, with a weighty name in the previous age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xingzong had been Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Master of the Palace with the Staff of Three Divisions under Song, a man of great standing in the previous dynasty.

sentences.zh: 撙少方雅退默，與兄寅俱知名。

translations.literal: Zun in youth was square, refined, retiring, and silent; he and his elder brother Yin were both well known.
translations.idiomatic: Zun in youth was upright, refined, retiring, and quiet; he and his elder brother Yin were both well known.

sentences.zh: 選補國子生，舉高第，爲司徒法曹行參軍。

translations.literal: He was selected and appointed a student of the Imperial Academy, graduated with highest honors, and became Acting Adjutant in the Law Bureau of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a student of the Imperial Academy, graduated with highest honors, and became Acting Adjutant in the Law Bureau of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 齊左衛將軍王儉高選府僚，以撙爲主簿。

translations.literal: Wang Jian, General of the Left Guard of Qi, made a rigorous selection of staff; he appointed Zun as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, General of the Left Guard of Qi, chose his staff with great care and appointed Zun chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 累遷建安王文學，司徒主簿、左西屬。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Literary Adjunct to the Prince of Jian'an, Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works, and Left Western Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Literary Adjunct to the Prince of Jian'an, chief clerk to the Minister of Works, and Left Western Assistant.

sentences.zh: 明帝爲鎮軍將軍，引爲從事中郎，遷中書侍郎，中軍長史，給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was General Who Guards the Army, he summoned him as Attendant-in-Ordinary on his staff, promoted him to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Chief Clerk to the Central Army, and Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming served as General Who Guards the Army, he summoned Zun as Attendant-in-Ordinary on his staff, then promoted him to Vice Director of the Secretariat, chief clerk to the Central Army, and Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，廬於墓側。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he built a hut beside her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he built a hut beside her tomb.

sentences.zh: 齊末多難，服闋，因居墓所。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi there were many troubles; when mourning ended he continued to dwell at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Qi’s final years were full of turmoil; when mourning ended he continued to live at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 除太子中庶子，太尉長史，並不就。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant, but accepted neither post.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and chief clerk to the Grand Commandant, but accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，爲侍中，遷臨海太守，坐公事左遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was established he became Attendant-in-Ordinary, then Administrator of Linhai; for an official matter he was demoted to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was established he became Attendant-in-Ordinary, then Administrator of Linhai; for an official matter he was demoted to Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 復爲侍中，吳興太守。

translations.literal: He again became Attendant-in-Ordinary and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Attendant-in-Ordinary and Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 天監九年，宣城郡吏吳承伯挾祅道聚衆攻宣城，殺太守朱僧勇。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianjian, Wu Chengbo, a clerk of Xuancheng Commandery, relied on heterodox teachings to gather a crowd and attack Xuancheng, killing the Administrator Zhu Sengyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Tianjian, Wu Chengbo, a clerk of Xuancheng Commandery, used heterodox teachings to gather a mob and attack Xuancheng, killing Administrator Zhu Sengyong.

sentences.zh: 因轉屠旁縣，逾山寇吳興，所過皆殘破，衆有二萬，奄襲郡城。

translations.literal: He then turned to slaughter the neighboring counties, crossed the mountains to raid Wuxing, ravaging everywhere he passed; his force numbered twenty thousand, and he suddenly struck the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to slaughter neighboring counties, crossed the mountains to raid Wuxing, and ravaged every place he passed; his force reached twenty thousand men, and he suddenly struck the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 東道不習兵革，吏民恇擾奔散，並請撙避之。

translations.literal: The eastern circuit was unused to arms; officials and people panicked and fled, all begging Zun to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern circuit was unused to war; officials and people panicked and fled, all begging Zun to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 撙堅守不動，募勇敢固郡。

translations.literal: Zun held firm without moving and recruited the brave to defend the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zun held firm without moving and recruited the brave to defend the commandery.

sentences.zh: 承伯盡銳攻撙，撙命衆出拒，戰於門，應手摧破，臨陣斬承伯，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Chengbo attacked Zun with his full strength; Zun ordered his men out to resist, fought at the gate, broke the enemy at the first clash, beheaded Chengbo on the field, and the remaining band was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chengbo attacked with his full strength; Zun ordered his men out to resist, fought at the gate, broke the enemy at the first clash, beheaded Chengbo on the field, and the remaining band was entirely pacified.

sentences.zh: 加信武將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of Trustworthy Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Trustworthy Martiality.

sentences.zh: 徵度支尚書，遷中書令。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Revenue and transferred to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Minister of Revenue and transferred to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 復爲信武將軍、晉陵太守。

translations.literal: He again became General of Trustworthy Martiality and Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He again became General of Trustworthy Martiality and Administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 還，除通直散騎常侍、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary Directly Attached and Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary Directly Attached and Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，居選，弘簡有名稱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel; in office over selections he was broad and simple, with a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel; in handling appointments he was broad and simple, and won a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 又爲侍中，領秘書監，轉中書令，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He again became Attendant Gentleman, headed the Directorate of the Secretariat, was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, and remained Attendant Gentleman as before.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Attendant Gentleman and Director of the Secretariat, retaining Attendant Gentleman while taking up the directorship.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，出爲宣毅將軍、吳郡太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong he went out as General of Manifest Resolution and Administrator of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Putong he was posted as General of Manifest Resolution and Administrator of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，時年五十七。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died, at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、金紫光祿大夫、宣惠將軍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Attendant Gentleman, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and General of Manifest Favor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Attendant Gentleman, Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and General of Manifest Favor.

sentences.zh: 諡康子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Marquis Kang.

sentences.zh: 子彥熙，歷官中書郎，宣城內史。

translations.literal: His son Yanxi held office in succession as Gentleman in the Secretariat and Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanxi served as Gentleman in the Secretariat and Administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 江蒨字彥標，濟陽考城人。

translations.literal: Jiang Qian, styled Yanbiao, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qian, whose style was Yanbiao, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖湛，宋左光祿、儀同三司；

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zhan was Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Master with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zhan had been Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under Song with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 父斅，齊太常卿：並有重名於前世。

translations.literal: His father Xiao was Grand Minister of Ceremonies of Qi—both men enjoyed great renown in earlier generations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiao had been Grand Minister of Ceremonies of Qi; both forebears enjoyed great fame.

sentences.zh: 蒨幼聰警，讀書過目便能諷誦。

translations.literal: Qian in youth was clever and alert; what he read he could recite after a single perusal.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Qian was quick and sharp; he could recite a text after reading it once.

sentences.zh: 選爲國子生，通《尚書》，舉高第。

translations.literal: He was chosen as a student at the Imperial University, mastered the Documents, and ranked at the top of his class.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial University, mastered the Documents, and graduated at the head of his class.

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，累遷司徒東閣祭酒、廬陵王主簿。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretary, and was promoted in succession to Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Sikong and Chief Clerk to the Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Secretary, then rose to libationer of the Sikong's Eastern Pavilion and chief clerk to the Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 居父憂以孝聞，廬於墓側，明帝敕遣齊仗二十人防墓所。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his father he became known for filial conduct and dwelt beside the tomb. Emperor Ming ordered twenty guards from Qi's army to protect the burial site.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his father, he won fame for filial devotion and lived beside the tomb; Emperor Ming sent twenty Qi guards to watch over the grave.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除太子洗馬，累遷司徒左南屬，太子中舍人，秘書丞。

translations.literal: When the mourning ended he was made Groom of the Heir Apparent and was promoted in succession to Left Aide of the South in the Sikong's office, Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became Groom of the Heir Apparent, then left aide in the Sikong's office, Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent, and Secretary.

sentences.zh: 出爲建安內史，視事朞月，義師下次江州，遣寧朔將軍劉諓之爲郡，蒨帥吏民據郡拒之。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Jian'an. After one month in office the righteous army reached Jiangzhou below. Ning Shuo General Liu Yanzhi was sent to take the commandery, and Qian led officials and people to hold the commandery and resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as Administrator of Jian'an, within a month the righteous army arrived at Jiangzhou. Liu Yanzhi, General Who Pacifies the North, was sent to take the commandery, and Qian led officials and people in its defense.

sentences.zh: 及建康城平，蒨坐禁錮。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Qian was placed under detention.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell, Qian was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 俄被原，起爲後軍臨川王外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was pardoned and appointed External Military Gentleman to the Prince of Linchuan, Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon pardoned, he became external military gentleman on the staff of Prince Linchuan of the Rear Army.

sentences.zh: 累遷臨川王友，中書侍郎，太子家令，黃門侍郎，領南兗州大中正。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Companion to the Prince of Linchuan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, Household Head to the Heir Apparent, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, and Chief Rectifier of Southern Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through companion to the Prince of Linchuan, Vice Director of the Secretariat, household head to the Heir Apparent, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, and chief rectifier of Southern Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中庶子，中正如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent, remaining Chief Rectifier as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Household Attendant to the Heir Apparent while keeping the chief rectifier's post.

sentences.zh: 轉中權始興王長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk to the Prince of Shixing, Central Authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk to Prince Shixing of the Central Authority.

sentences.zh: 出爲伏波將軍、晉安內史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Subdues Waves and Administrator of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as General Who Subdues Waves and Administrator of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 在政清約，務在寬惠，吏民便之。

translations.literal: In government he was pure and sparing, striving for leniency and kindness, to the convenience of officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with austerity and kindness, to the ease of officials and people alike.

sentences.zh: 詔徵爲寧朔將軍、南康王長史，行府、州、國事。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him as General Who Pacifies the North, Chief Clerk to the Prince of Nankang, acting for the fief, commandery, and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as General Who Pacifies the North and chief clerk to the Prince of Nankang, acting for the fief, commandery, and state.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷太尉臨川王長史，轉尚書吏部郎，右將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Chief Clerk to the Prince of Linchuan, Grand Commandant, transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, and General of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became chief clerk to Prince Linchuan, Grand Commandant, then Vice Minister of Personnel and General of the Right.

sentences.zh: 蒨方雅有風格。

translations.literal: Qian was by nature refined and possessed style.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was refined and possessed real style.

sentences.zh: 僕射徐勉以權重自遇，在位者並宿士敬之，惟蒨及王規與抗禮，不爲之屈。

translations.literal: Vice Director Xu Mian treated men according to his own weight in power; those in office, all veterans, honored him, but only Qian and Wang Gui matched him in ceremony and did not bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Mian threw his weight around; senior officials deferred to him, but only Qian and Wang Gui met him as equals and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 勉因蒨門客翟景爲第七兒繇求蒨女婚，蒨不答，景再言之，乃杖景四十，由此與勉有忤。

translations.literal: Mian, through Qian's client Zhai Jing, sought Qian's daughter in marriage for his seventh son Yao. Qian did not answer; when Jing spoke again, Qian had Jing beaten forty strokes. From this he was at odds with Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Through Qian's client Zhai Jing, Mian sought Qian's daughter for his seventh son Yao. Qian ignored him; when Jing pressed again, Qian had Jing beaten forty strokes and fell out with Mian.

sentences.zh: 除散騎常侍，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Offered Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, he declined.

sentences.zh: 是時勉又爲子求蒨弟葺及王泰女，二人並拒之。

translations.literal: At that time Mian again sought Qian's younger brother Qi and Wang Tai's daughters in marriage for his son; both men refused.
translations.idiomatic: Mian then sought Qian's brother Qi and Wang Tai's daughter for his son; both refused.

sentences.zh: 葺爲吏部郎，坐杖曹中幹免官，泰以疾假出宅，乃遷散騎常侍，皆勉意也。

translations.literal: Qi was Vice Minister of Personnel and was dismissed for beating a clerk in the ministry; Tai took sick leave and left his residence. Both were then transferred to Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry—all at Mian's instigation.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, as Vice Minister of Personnel, was dismissed for beating a ministry clerk; Tai left his house on medical leave. Both were moved to Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry—at Mian's doing.

sentences.zh: 初，天監六年，詔以侍中、常侍並侍帷幄，分門下二局入集書，其官品視侍中，而非華胄所悅，故勉斥泰爲之。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the sixth year of Tianjian, an edict had made Attendant Gentlemen and Palace Attendants attend within the curtain, dividing the two bureaus of the Masters of Writing into the Imperial Library, with rank equal to Attendant Gentlemen—yet this was not pleasing to eminent clans, and so Mian pushed Tai into it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjian an edict had Attendant Gentlemen and Palace Attendants attend within the curtain and merged two Masters of Writing bureaus into the Imperial Library at their rank—unwelcome to great families, and Mian used it to sideline Tai.

sentences.zh: 蒨尋遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Qian was soon promoted to Left Chief Clerk of the Sikong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was soon made left chief clerk of the Sikong.

sentences.zh: 初，王泰出閤，高祖謂勉云：「江蒨資歷，應居選部。

translations.literal: When Wang Tai left the Secretariat, the High Ancestor said to Mian, "Jiang Qian's qualifications should place him in the Ministry of Personnel."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tai left the Secretariat, the High Ancestor told Mian, "Jiang Qian's qualifications suit the Ministry of Personnel."

sentences.zh: 」勉對曰：「蒨有眼患，又不悉人物。

translations.literal: Mian replied, "Qian has an eye ailment and does not know men well."
translations.idiomatic: Mian answered, "Qian has eye trouble and does not know men well."

sentences.zh: 」高祖乃止。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Qian was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 大通元年，卒，時年五十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he died, at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 詔贈本官。

translations.literal: An edict granted his former office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted his former rank.

sentences.zh: 諡肅子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Marquis Su.

sentences.zh: 蒨好學，尤悉朝儀故事，撰《江左遺典》三十卷，未就，卒。

translations.literal: Qian loved learning and was especially versed in court ritual and precedent. He compiled thirty juan of Remnant Institutions of the Eastern Court, but did not finish before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Qian loved learning and knew court ritual and precedent especially well. He drafted thirty juan of Remnant Institutions of the Eastern Court but died before finishing.

sentences.zh: 文集十五卷。

translations.literal: His collected writings were fifteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to fifteen juan.

sentences.zh: 子紑、經，在《孝行傳》。

translations.literal: His sons Zhou and Jing are treated in the Biography of Filial Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhou and Jing appear in the Biography of Filial Conduct.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：王氏自姬姓已降，及乎秦漢，繼有英哲。

translations.literal: The historian says: From the time the Wang clan descended from the Ji surname down through Qin and Han, worthy men appeared in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: From the Ji clan down through Qin and Han, the Wangs produced worthy men in succession.

sentences.zh: 洎東晉王茂弘經綸江左，時人方之管仲。

translations.literal: By the Eastern Jin, Wang Maohong governed the lands east of the Yangtze, and men of the time compared him to Guan Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: By the Eastern Jin, Wang Maohong governed the lands east of the Yangtze, and contemporaries compared him to Guan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 其後蟬冕交映，台袞相襲，勒名帝籍，慶流子孫，斯爲盛族矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter court caps and robes shone upon one another, terrace and grandee garments passed in succession, names were carved on the imperial registers, and blessings flowed to sons and grandsons—such was this great clan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter court caps and robes glittered in succession, high office passed from father to son, names were entered on the imperial registers, and blessing flowed to descendants—such was this great house.

sentences.zh: 王瞻等承藉茲基，國華是貴，子有才行，可得而稱。

translations.literal: Wang Zhan and the others inherited this foundation; national splendor was their birthright, and their sons possessed talent and conduct that may be spoken of with praise.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan and the others inherited this foundation; national glory was their birthright, and their sons had talent and conduct worth praising.

sentences.zh: 張充少不持操，晚乃折節，在於典選，實號廉平。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong in youth did not hold to conduct, but in later years greatly restrained himself; in charge of selection he was truly called fair and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong neglected propriety in youth but greatly reformed in later years; in appointments he was truly called fair and upright.

sentences.zh: 柳惲以多藝稱，蔡撙以方雅著，江蒨以風格顯，俱爲梁室名士焉。

translations.literal: Liu Yun was famed for many arts, Cai Zun noted for square elegance, Jiang Qian distinguished for style—all were celebrated gentlemen of the Liang house.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun was famed for many arts, Cai Zun for square elegance, Jiang Qian for style—all were celebrated gentlemen of Liang.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker in the source text.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七三年五月版《梁書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang of May 1973.
translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang (May 1973).
